Tech Report: What's next for the Twins? Three things Minnesota must do to make a postseason push in 2027 season

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1114 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that it has been a surprisingly productive week for the Minnesota Twins.
  • It has been revealed that then, on Wednesday, the Twins brought back veteran righty Sonny Gray with a two-year contract worth $55 million.
  • "I really don't take it lightly that he chose us," GM Jeremy Zoll told the Associated Press about Gray's return.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that it has been a surprisingly productive week for the Minnesota Twins. First, catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer on Tuesday. Jeffers turned down a multi-year offer from the Twins, according to The Athletic, so he's betting on himself. Betting that he'll at least maintain his free agent stock and get paid next offseason.

It has been revealed that then, on Wednesday, the Twins brought back veteran righty Sonny Gray with a two-year contract worth $55 million. There's an opt-out after the first year. Gray, 37, finished fifth in the AL Cy Young voting this season and pitched wonderfully for the Twins in 2022 and 2023. He joins a rotation that, on paper, looks like one of the better starting units in the American League.

Here is Minnesota's rotation depth chart:.

"I really don't take it lightly that he chose us," GM Jeremy Zoll told the Associated Press about Gray's return. "He had an abundance of options, and given where he's at in his career, I know how notable it is to him. He expressed it quite directly how important it is to win, and this isn't just about having a good season or a winning season. It's about winning and going deep in the playoffs and making a real playoff run.".

Recent findings suggest that matthews could land in the bullpen next season and that might be his long-term home. His stuff should be well suited to a relief role. Gray makes the rotation better and potentially the bullpen better as well by bumping Matthews to relief. Jeffers accepting the qualifying offer keeps a key middle-of-the-order bat in place. A good week for the Twins, this has been.

Sources indicate that after a disappointing 77-85 finish this year, Minnesota has already improved significantly in the early days of the offseason. They play in the AL Central. With all due respect, it is not the most imposing division. There's no reason the Twins can't be in the division and wild card races next season. Here now is what's left on Minnesota's offseason to-do list.

It has been revealed that teams had until 5 p.m. ET Friday to offer their pre-arbitration and arbitration-eligible players contracts for 2027. They didn't have to sign them Friday, but they had to tender an offer; otherwise, the player immediately became a free agent. Dozens of players were cut loose at the non-tender deadline, as usual, and two players stood out as non-tender candidates for the Twins: Trevor Larnach and Royce Lewis. Larnach was indeed non-tendered, while Lewis was dealt to the Dodgers.

It has been revealed that it's not often a player gets non-tendered after posting a .352 on-base percentage and 120 OPS+, but the writing was on the wall. The Twins had an agreement in place to trade Larnach at the deadline (Astros owner Jim Crane nixed the deal) and they have a very crowded outfield. Also, Larnach had wrist surgery earlier this month. That created some questions going into next season, and the Twins opted to cut him loose.

According to recent reports, larnach had one more year of control remaining and was expected to make over $6 million through arbitration in 2027. I reckon the Twins tried again to trade him prior to Friday's non-tender deadline. In the end, he was non-tendered rather than risk tying $6 million or so up in yet another outfielder, particularly one who is coming off wrist surgery.

Things got so bad this summer that Lewis, who has a .288 on-base percentage in over 1,200 plate appearances the last three years, was sent to Triple-A for a spell, and also moved across the diamond from third base to first base. The Twins could not count on him to provide offense and now he's playing a position with a high offensive bar. That made him expendable.

Lewis, 27, was under team control through 2028 and that extra year was an important consideration for the club. His salary would have been in the $5 million range next season through arbitration, which is pricey but not exorbitant. Now, Lewis will receive a fresh start with the Dodgers, where he can be one of the guys, not the former No. 1 overall pick and expected face of the franchise.

According to recent reports, the Twins presumably did not want to give up on a player with as much talent as Lewis. At the same time, they kept trying, and it never worked.

Sources indicate that the Twins got a head start on their offseason bullpen shopping when they acquired Jeff Hoffman at the trade deadline. He has one more year remaining on the contract and will be in the team's late-inning mix in 2027.

Here is manager Derek Shelton's bullpen unit at the moment:.

Recent findings suggest that morris is not yet a household name, but he has a great arm and was dominant at times in 2026. The Twins have themselves a nice little late-inning trio in Gómez, Hoffman, and Morris. A spare starter like Matthews or Prielipp could wind up in the bullpen as well. Given the quality of their stuff, they have a chance to make a real impact as relievers.

It has been revealed that clearly though, the middle relief could use some help, and the Twins wouldn't need to spend big dollars to improve it. A second-tier free agent like, say, Andrew Kittredge would be a solid pickup. It's worth giving the Miami Marlins a call to see what it would take to get Anthony Bender and/or Michael Petersen. Point is, the bullpen can be improved, for sure.

The Twins have way more outfielders than outfield spots and that is in no way a bad thing. First and foremost, it allows them to use Byron Buxton as the full-time DH, which could help keep him on the field. Secondly, there's no such thing as too many good players. Depth is vital and the Twins certainly have plenty of it in the outfield.

It has been revealed that more outfielders than outfield spots is not a problem. It's just something the Twins have to figure out. Even if we assume Buxton will DH and is not part of the outfield mix, here are the outfielders Minnesota must sort through:.

Rodriguez is one of the game's 50 or so best prospects and he is out of minor league options, meaning he must go through waivers to go to Triple-A. Obviously, the Twins won't waive him. Non-tendering Larnach allows the Twins to play Rodriguez alongside Jenkins and Keaschall in the outfield, keep Kreidler and Martin on the bench, and keep the others in Triple-A.

Breaking: Connor Hellebuyck trade: Jets send star goalie to the Devils in exchange for four players, two draft picks

📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1141 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil.
  • Industry observers note that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August.
  • According to recent reports, hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, connor Hellebuyck is a now a Devil. The star goalie for the Winnipeg Jets is on the move after being traded to New Jersey on Friday in exchange for four players and two future draft picks. the teams declared the move with the Jets receiving Dawson Mercer, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws and Alexander Command, plus a 2027 seventh-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick.

Industry observers note that hellebuyck expressed his desire to be traded in the offseason when he formally requested a move in August. He remarked at the time that he had made the request months earlier and tried to keep the situation private.

According to recent reports, hellebuyck has spent his entire career with Winnipeg after being drafted by the Jets in 2012 at No. 130 overall. He's recognized as one of the best goalies in the league as a three-time Vezina Trophy winner. He also helped carry the United States to its first gold medal since 1980 at the 2026 Olympics in February with some incredible saves against Canada in the final game.

After trading Jacob Markstom in the offseason, the Devils had a clear need in goal, and this splashy move certainly fills that need. With a talented young core already in place, New Jersey's Stanley Cup window is wide open.

RAISE HELLE!Connor Hellebuyck is a Fresh Jersey Devil: https://t.co/HCehRGOQI5 pic.twitter.com/dZGNQR16m1.

For the Jets, it must be a hard pill to swallow when a franchise icon decides to walk out they door, but this trade package should help them as the enter a upcoming era and revamp the roster. Winnipeg got a former first-rounder in Mercer to try and add to a rebuild as well as a veteran presence in Bjugstad. They also acquired a younger goalie in Daws who could fill the role of Hellebuyck at just 25 years old.

Goaltending has been an matter in New Jersey for a while now -- even after the team acquired Markstrom from the Calgary Flames in 2024. Markstom never really panned out, and his 13.6 goals allowed above average, per Natural Stat Trick, were a massive reason why the Devils missed the postseason last year.

It has been revealed that in the early portion of this season, it was clear that New Jersey needed to make a move to upgrade in the crease. Daws and veteran Jake Allen simply aren't a tandem suitable for a Stanley Cup contender, and the numbers backed that up. New Jersey ranks 24th in team save percentage at .877, and the duo of Daws and Allen combined to surrender 2.99 goals above average.

Once Hellebuyck gets up to game speed, that shouldn't be a problem anymore.

Sources indicate that in the three-season stretch from 2023-26, Hellebuyck led the NHL with 73.42 goals saved above average, which is 20 goals higher than the next closest netminder. Over that span, Hellebuyck also posted a standard save percentage of .914 and an astronomical high-danger save-percentage of .832.

Hellebuyck carried less talented teams to the playoffs multiple times in his career. Now on a team loaded with weaponry in their prime -- Jack Hughes, Jesper Bratt and Nico Hischier to name a few -- Hellebuyck could be the final piece to the championship puzzle.

In terms of the acquisition cost, it was probably an easy deal for Devils general manager Sunny Mehta to make. The 2029 second-round pick is useless for a team that should be all-in now, Bjugstad is simply a depth piece and Daws now has no path to a starting role with Hellebuyck in town.

The most interesting trade chips are Mercer and Command. Mercer flashed major upside with 56 points in his second NHL season, 2022-23, but he hasn't really come close to hitting those heights again. Still, even if he has plateaued, Mercer remains a strong middle-six forward rising into his prime.

Although Command had his detractors -- and may have been over-drafted at No. 12 overall -- he was a consensus first-round pick last summer. That gives Winnipeg a potential franchise forward it can build around long-term, but Newly introduced Jersey already has one of the deepest forward groups in the league, especially with the emergence of Arseny Gritsyuk and the acquisition of Luke Evangelista.

In a recent development, if we're looking for a 3-D chess angle of this deal, it only makes the Devils more appealing for a certain Minnesota Wild defenseman whose brothers just happen to play in New Jersey already. Grade -- A+.

Let's get the obvious out of the way first: The Jets were never going to get fair value for Hellebuyck because, at his best, he's the No. 1 goaltender in the world with no equal. That type of excellence can't be replaced.

That remarked, Winnipeg did fairly well given the circumstances. Hellebuyck made a public trade request, and he wasn't even with the team after sitting out for the entirety of training camp. The entire league knew the Jets had to trade him.

Hellebuyck's talent created a decent market anyway, but most of the suitors were bona fide Stanley Cup contenders with little in the way of valuable draft capital, and they weren't going to knee cap the roster by sending a key player back in return.

Industry observers note that with all that taken into consideration, Kevin Cheveldayoff got a solid return. Although Mercer's ceiling may be lower than initially thought, he's a 24-year-old forward who banks roughly 20 goals and 20 assists every season. The kicker with Mercer will be Winnipeg's ability to re-sign him before he hits restricted free agency next summer.

Industry observers note that the addition of Command means Winnipeg now has two forwards selected in the top 12 of the 2026 NHL Draft after taking center Viggo Bjorck themselves. If both of those players deliver on their first-round pedigrees, they could be a terrific one-two punch for the team long-term.

Daws was a third-round pick in 2020, and despite playing just 13 NHL games since the start of the 2024-25 season, he should give Winnipeg a solid back up option behind Stuart Skinner. It certainly helps that Skinner is off to a great start with his new team -- and if Daws develops into a true No. 1 -- it'll be gravy.

In a recent development, if there's any reason to critique this deal from the Jets' side of things, it's that they didn't get premium draft capital or a surefire up-and-coming prospect. Maybe Command develops into a star, but there's no guarantee he becomes a top-six stud in the NHL.

The Jets got a lot of good stuff, but they didn't really get anything great, at least not based on what we know in the moment. Because of that, I have to ding Winnipeg a little bit. Grade: B.

Royce Lewis trade grades: Dodgers land former No. 1 pick; Twins get another arm, arrow-up prospect

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (601 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No.
  • In a recent development, lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline.
  • According to recent reports, the Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No. 1 overall pick. The Dodgers are set to acquire infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins for right-hander Bobby Miller and minor-league catcher Francisco Espinoza, reports the Newly introduced York Post. Neither team has announced the trade.

In a recent development, lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline. Rather than cut him loose, the Twins were able to find a trade partner and receive something in return. The No. 1 pick in the 2017 draft has battled injuries throughout his career and posted a .288 on-base percentage the last three years. Lewis simply failed to launch with Minnesota.

According to recent reports, the Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy. The Twins moved him from third base to first base this past season. Lewis has played every infield position in the big leagues, though he's had only one inning at shortstop since 2022.

Sources indicate that miller, 27, has been unable to build on his dynamic 2022 rookie season, when he threw 124 ⅓ innings with a 3.76 ERA. He has battled injuries and control complications since then, and the Dodgers moved him into the bullpen this past season. Miller has a 7.75 ERA in 134 ⅔ Triple-A innings the last three years and can be optioned down in 2027.

Espinoza, 19, reached Low Class-A in 2026 and hit .317/.411/.422 with three home runs and strong contact rates in 46 games. He does not rank among the top 30 Dodgers prospects at Baseball America or MLB Pipeline, but Espinoza is an arrow-up prospect and a solid return for a non-tender candidate.

Here now are our grades for the two-for-one trade.

At worst, Lewis will be a high-priced utility guy next season. He's projected to make $5 million or so through arbitration and that simply is not much for the Dodgers, who have a history of getting underperforming hitters to the next level (like Muncy). At best, Lewis could be the fresh Chris Taylor and reach his offensive ceiling while bouncing between positions.

Industry observers note that espinoza is a good prospect, not a great prospect, and Miller is a reclamation project. Those are easy players for the Dodgers to surrender to take a chance on Lewis and his upside. It may not work. Lewis could continue to get hurt and not hit, but it was a low-cost move and the chance of a reward is significant.

It's a very nice upside play for a team that has hit on a lot of upside plays over the year.

It's a bummer things didn't work out for Lewis and the Twins, but the reality is he was a non-tender candidate, and it wasn't a secret. Minnesota was able to get back a solid prospect in Espinoza and a lottery ticket arm in Miller despite having little leverage. Getting two players for Lewis is a very good outcome under the circumstances.

Sources indicate that giving each team an "A" suggests a win-win, and maybe it will be. There's a chance it's a lose-lose, though. Lewis may not hit, Miller may never rediscover his 2022 form, and Espinoza may not pan out. I see the vision for both teams, though and like it.

The Dodgers rolled the dice on a talented player and the Twins were able to fetch two players for someone they might have otherwise cut loose and sent into free agency.

    MLB rumors: Yankees moves heating up, plus latest on Tarik Skubal, Mets, Padres, Red Sox, more

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1094 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway.
    • According to recent reports, thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing.
    • According to recent reports, the buzz at the GM Meetings last week was that the Mets offered top free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth almost $400 million, reports MLB Network Radio.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near-certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free-agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples.

    According to recent reports, thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Friday's supply just below.

    According to recent reports, the buzz at the GM Meetings last week was that the Mets offered top free agent Tarik Skubal a nine-year contract worth almost $400 million, reports MLB Network Radio. If the deal is worth at least $390 million, it would set fresh records for total guarantee and average annual value given to a pitcher. Here are the current pitcher contract records:.

    1. Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers: $325M.

    2. Justin Verlander, Mets: $43.3M.

    3. Stephen Strasburg, Nationals: $245M.

    3. Zack Wheeler, Phillies: $42M.

    4. Framber Valdez, Tigers: $38.3M.

    Given the player and the deep-pocketed teams involved in the bidding (Blue Jays, Dodgers, Mets, etc.), Skubal is well-positioned to shatter Yamamoto's record. He could beat Scherzer's and Verlander's record as well. The expected lockout will begin after the collective bargaining agreement expires at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Skubal is likely to sign before then.

    The Diamondbacks are set to acquire righty Johan Oviedo from the Red Sox for minor-league lefty Luke Dotson and a player to be named later, reports the Arizona Republic. Boston had four pitchers for the No. 5 starter's spot (Oviedo, Brayan Bello, Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck) and always seemed likely to trade one to ease the logjam.

    In a recent development, acquired from the Pirates last offseason, Oviedo made just one ineffective appearance around elbow trouble in 2026. He returned from Tommy John surgery in 2025 and looked excellent, and Arizona will hope Oviedo rediscovers that magic as he gets further away from his injuries. Dotson is not a top prospect. It's a low-cost flier for the D-backs.

    The Tigers have signed right-hander Troy Melton to a six-year extension worth $46.5 million, reports ESPN. There is a club option for a seventh year and escalators can push the total guarantee to $80 million. Melton still had five years of team control. The new extension buys out his five team control years and one free agent year with an option for another free agent year.

    Melton, 26 next month, missed the start of the season with elbow inflammation and finished the season on the injured list with more elbow woes. Between injuries, he made 20 starts with a sub-3.00 ERA with strong under-the-hood numbers. The Tigers know him better than anyone and are obviously comfortable with Melton's medicals to lock him up long-term.

    Industry observers note that the Upcoming York Yankees have agreed to a two-year contract with veteran right-hander Jonathan Loáisiga, ESPN reports. The deal also includes a club option for 2029 and is worth roughly $18 million, according to MLB.com.

    Loáisiga, 32, is coming off that strong season above for the Arizona Diamondbacks, and for his career boasts an ERA+ of 128 across parts of nine MLB seasons. He's worked in relief for almost all of that span, and eight of those nine seasons came with the Yankees.

    New York Yankees general manager Brian Cashman was recently asked if he'd be willing to play Spencer Jones in center field. In response, he told media, including SNY, this:.

    Recent findings suggest that "I would be comfortable with that. At the same time Jasson Domínguez is pounding the ball in winter ball. The entire industry is noticing that based on the phone calls I'm getting.".

    The 23-year-old Domínguez still has big-time power potential, and defensively he's best suited to center field. For his career in the Bronx, he has an OPS+ of 93, but his 751 plate appearances have been doled out erratically across four seasons. As things stand now, he'll once again be subject to a playing-time crunch. Aaron Judge and Cody Bellinger are installed at the outfield corners, and Giancarlo Stanton, if healthy, should get much of the playing time at DH. That leaves center field for Jones or Domínguez. Other teams no doubt see that bottleneck and are seeing if Cashman and the Yankees are willing to relieve it through trade.

    Sources indicate that lefty ace and two-time American League Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal remains far and away the top talent on the free-agent market. While the New York Mets and incumbent Los Angeles Dodgers seem like the favorites to secure his services, the San Diego Padres also have significant interest in him. That interest took the next step on Thursday with an in-person meeting, The Athletic reports. The Padres are the fourth team to meet with Skubal, who turned 30 on Friday. Previously, the Dodgers, Mets, and Toronto Blue Jays met with him.

    It has been revealed that the Padres have a pronounced need in the rotation, especially if free-agent right-hander Michael King signs elsewhere. Last winter, they also lost Dylan Cease to the Blue Jays via free agency.

    The Padres and left-handed platoon hitter Gavin Sheets have agreed to a three-year, $11 million contract extension that includes two opt-outs, FanSided reports. Sheets, who'll turn 31 in April, had been slated for free agency after the upcoming season. Instead, he and the Padres will now be potentially committed through the 2029 season, depending on whether Sheets exercises any of his opt-outs. While he's not much of a hitter for average, he does draw walks and hit for power. In two seasons with San Diego, he's tallied 36 home runs and 44 doubles in 855 at-bats while seeing DH, first base, and the outfield corners.

    The New York Mets have agreed to a three-year, $12 million deal with right-handed reliever Darwinzon Hernández, reports José F. Rivera.

    Industry observers note that hernández, who turns 30 in December, hasn't pitched in MLB since 2022 and instead has revived his career with four strong seasons in Japan. Over that span for Softbank of the NPB, he's put up an ERA of 2.46 in 131 ⅔ innings with 168 strikeouts and 42 unintentional walks. Prior to rebuilding himself in Japan, Hernández had a 5.06 ERA and a 1.82 K/BB ratio over parts of four seasons with the Boston Red Sox.

    Latest Update: NBA's eight biggest disappointments through one month: Injury bug, same old East and an underwhelming champ

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that we're roughly one month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and things are going pretty well in certain respects.
    • Industry observers note that in other areas, things are going … not so well.
    • Industry observers note that there have been so many players impacted by various injuries that it's almost hard to keep track.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that we're roughly one month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and things are going pretty well in certain respects. Luka Dončić and the Lakers are off to a hot start in Los Angeles. Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs have picked up right where they left off after last season's Finals trip. And the Celtics are battling the fresh-look Sixers at the top of the Eastern Conference.

    Industry observers note that in other areas, things are going … not so well. Below are the eight biggest disappointments so far this season.

    Industry observers note that there have been so many players impacted by various injuries that it's almost hard to keep track. Jalen Duren (hamstring) has missed almost the entire season in Detroit. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are still recovering from knee injuries and have yet to play for Golden State, while Steph Curry is now out with an abdominal tear and Kristaps Porziņģis stepped away from basketball. After sitting out all of last season with an Achilles tear, Tyrese Haliburton is currently dealing with a hamstring concern. Brandon Ingram (Achilles) hasn't made his debut for the Clippers. Austin Reaves is out with a heel injury. Anthony Edwards underwent knee surgery and will miss a chunk of time for the Wolves, and it seems unlikely that Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) will play this season, even though he remains hopeful that he will. Paolo Banchero remains sidelined with an ankle sprain. Ja Morant is out with a hamstring strain. Ben Simmons didn't play a single game for the Kings before tearing his Achilles. Kawhi Leonard (knee) is once again on the shelf in Toronto. And the reeling Jazz are without Jaren Jackson Jr (knee), Lauri Markkanen (hand) and Jusuf Nurkic (toe).

    According to recent reports, it's all a huge bummer for the players, their teams and fans of hoops in general. But no team has been hurt more on the injury front than the Thunder.

    The disappointment here is how unkind fate has been to OKC. The Thunder were close to fully healthy when the season started — and then far from it not long after it began. When OKC beat the Spurs in San Antonio in the season opener — after losing four of five regular season games to them last season, as well as falling to the Spurs in the Western Conference Finals — it felt like a statement that the Thunder were back and we were in for an epic battle between the two teams over who would rule the West.

    And then all of that was stripped away. Just three games into the season, Jalen Williams — who missed much of last season due to injury — suffered a gruesome fall and had to undergo surgery for a fractured fibula as well as reconstruction of ankle ligaments. In that same fateful game, Cason Wallace tore his labrum and later had shoulder surgery. They haven't been officially ruled out, but if either of them plays basketball again this season, it will be a surprise. Making matters worse, Chet Holmgren tore a tendon in his knee and "underwent a biological treatment" to address it. He'll miss approximately two months, but the Thunder do expect him to return. That's what passes for good news in OKC these days.

    Industry observers note that the Thunder are — or were — the deepest team in the NBA. That's a credit to what Sam Presti built. But even OKC has its limits. Losing three of five starters is tough to overcome, even when you're led by the reigning back-to-back MVP in Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. That doesn't mean the Thunder (currently 9-6 and eighth in the West) can't still make a deep playoff run, but the odds of them doing so — and of them fighting the Spurs all season for the top spot — got a lot longer.

    We were told that this was finally the season that the East returned to its former glory. We were told that the conference would be loaded. We were wrong. (Full disclosure while putting a palm to my face: I might have done some of that telling.).

    Industry observers note that through the first month, the East has been mostly underwhelming. Eight of the 15 teams are below .500. The conference has a combined 17-37 record against the West. Only one of the top seven teams in net rating — the Celtics — plays in the East. Five of the top six teams by point differential play in the West.

    The defending champion Knicks are 8-6. The Cavaliers, who made it to last season's Eastern Conference Finals and had championship aspirations of their own, are 8-8. The Magic, Raptors and Pacers — who presently occupy the eight, nine and 10 seeds — all have losing records. By contrast, the worst play-in team in the West right now is Golden State at 8-7. That record would be good enough for the seven seed if they played in the East.

    But maybe we shouldn't be surprised. Since the 1999-2000 season, the West has had the better overall record in all but three campaigns. Maybe next year the East will finally snap out of its funk, but don't bet on it.

    It has been revealed that the Jazz just picked up back-to-back road wins in L.A. over the Lakers and Clippers, but that doesn't begin to dig them out of the deep hole they've made for themselves. The Jazz were gearing up to be competitive in the West this season. So much for that. Like the Thunder, injuries have not been kind to them. Nurkic has yet to play a single game this season, while Markkanen and JJJ have missed significant time with maladies of their own. What looked like a formidable frontcourt has been decimated.

    Still, it's hard to believe how bad the Jazz have been in pretty much every facet. Their first win came in the second game of the season, a one-point squeaker over the Pelicans. It took until mid-November to end an ugly 12-game losing streak and pick up their second and third wins. They're 25th in net rating and point differential. The season has barely begun, and it's already basically wait until next year for the Jazz.

    Industry observers note that the NBA panicked and tried to solve for a problem that wasn't actually an matter, except for a small fragment of people who care more about optics than the product itself. And so the league enacted lottery reform and the fresh 3-2-1 system was put in place. This was ostensibly designed to prevent tanking, incentivize winning and bring greater parity to the league. Oops.

    The Hornets, Wizards, Bulls, Nets and Bucks are all well underwater in the East. The Pelicans and Clippers are drowning in the West, while the Kings and Jazz are even worse. What the league failed to account for is that some of these teams are just organically bad — and now they will have decreased odds at getting better.

    Sources indicate that under the old system, the Grizzlies would be pretty thrilled to see the Jazz struggling since Memphis has Utah's first-round pick in the upcoming draft as part of the JJJ trade. Alas, after making that move, the league changed the rules, which means the Grizzlies can pick no higher than sixth now as a consequence of the latest system preventing a team from picking in the top five in three consecutive drafts. Since the Jazz picked in the top five in each of the last two drafts, that means the Grizzlies are now out of luck with that Utah pick this time around. Womp, womp for them.

    And on top of it all, fans of bad teams were robbed of the entertaining-in-its-own-way race to the bottom to maximize lottery odds, giving supporters a small silver lining in the otherwise gray clouds of their season. RIP Tank Watch.

    According to recent reports, when aren't the Kings disappointing? Aside from their unsightly 1-13 record, the Sacramento front office continues to make baffling decisions. The Kings originally acquired Nique Clifford from the Thunder for a Spurs 2027 first-round pick. Sacramento held onto Clifford for 83 games — choosing to bury him on the bench this season and play him barely six minutes per game — before shipping him back to the Thunder for two second-round picks.

    So the Thunder ended up with the player and a first and the Kings ended up with two seconds.

    Industry observers note that one of these organizations is savvy and opportunistic, and the other is the Kings. It's a miracle they nailed the Darius Acuff pick.

    It has been revealed that oof. It has not been a good season to date for Bridges. After going cold to begin their first-round playoff series against the Hawks, Bridges found his form and played well, helping the Knicks go on an epic run that ended with New York's first championship in 53 years.

    According to recent reports, if that hope was that Bridges would snap out of his early-season funk in similar fashion, the Knicks seem somewhat less patient these days. While head coach Mike Brown has insisted that Bridges is a starter, he has sometimes hedged his bets in crucial situations, going with Landry Shamet or Deuce McBride over Bridges when things get tight and the Knicks need more reliable offense on the floor.

    According to recent reports, through 14 games, Bridges is averaging 7.5 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists on 40.2/28.9/75 shooting splits. It's the lowest scoring output and the worst shooting numbers of his career. As a result, his minutes have dipped to 25.6 per contest. That's also a career low. Bridges is still a plus defender. And he's only 30. The Knicks obviously hope he'll figure it out, as he has in the past. If not, his upcoming four-year, $150 million extension that kicked in this season will start to look worrisome.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, friday marked the non-tender deadline in Major League Baseball.
    • Most such decisions are easy and obvious.
    • Recent findings suggest that all that sets the stage for what follows, which is our list of the most compelling non-tendered players who are now on the market and available for hire.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, friday marked the non-tender deadline in Major League Baseball. That key date on the offseason calendar is when clubs must make, or "tender," contract offers for the upcoming season to all their arbitration-eligible and pre-arbitration players on the 40-player roster. That's every player who isn't a free agent or isn't presently signed to a multi-year contract. Players who are tendered a contract by that deadline remain with their current organizations. Players who aren't offered a contract become free agents.

    Most such decisions are easy and obvious. Others, however, present difficult calls for the organization because of roster crunches, crowded depth charts, or, more commonly, reluctance to retain a player as his salary rises through the arbitration process. While a number of non-tendered players are likely on their way out of the league, a select few others qualify as at least interesting to other teams and, on occasion, a few will even be coveted to varying degrees.

    Recent findings suggest that all that sets the stage for what follows, which is our list of the most compelling non-tendered players who are now on the market and available for hire. Let's get to it ….

    Sources indicate that the 2024 AL Rookie of the Year, Gil has been injured and ineffective the last two seasons. He missed time with a shoulder glitch this past season and also spent time in Triple-A. The Yankees moved him to the bullpen late in the season to see whether he could contribute that way, though Gil was unable to make a strong impression in that role. Now 28, Gil still has another three seasons of team control remaining. Whichever team signs him will be able to keep him through 2029, and that extra control, plus his Rookie of the Year pedigree, will no doubt land Gil with a new team before Opening Day.

    It has been revealed that as a 23-year-old in 2023, the infielder and former first-rounder hit 27 home runs in 119 games and looked like a future cornerstone for the Cardinals. Gorman, however, has gotten steadily worse since then thanks largely to his persistent strikeout complications. Last season, he wound up back at Triple-A for an extended stretch and didn't fare any better upon being recalled. Long-term, the Cardinals will likely look to hand the third base position to rising power prospect Jesús Báez, who was recently added to the 40-player roster. Gorman can be a plus at third and probably still get by at second, and no doubt some team will take a chance on his power.

    In a recent development, on the downside, Larnach is a defensive minus at the corner outfield spots and probably needs to be a DH, and he's also a platoon bat. On the upside, he's been a steady producer from the left side of the plate. This past season, he put up a .352 OBP and an OPS+ of 120 for Minnesota. For his career, he has an OPS+ of 106 across parts of six MLB seasons. He out-hit his underlying indicators by a bit in 2026, but Larnach is still going to be an appealing part-time bat for some teams.

    The Twins cut bait on a right-hander who's made 139 career starts for them since his 2021 big-league debut. Ober boasts a career OPS+ of 102, but that figure has slid over the last two seasons. What's also slid is Ober's fastball velocity, which may be why he's on this list. In his rookie season, he averaged a fringy 92.4 mph with his four-seamer, but last season that figure was down all the way to 88 mph. That put him in the very bottom percentile among MLB hurlers. The 31-year-old Ober still should draw some interest as a depth piece.

    A platoon extraordinaire, Raley has always hit for power against righties, including 15 home runs in only 290 plate appearances against them in 2026. He's sneaky fast and a very good athlete for his size (6-foot-3 and 235 lbs.), good enough to handle the corner outfield spots competently. Raley also has first base experience and can patrol center field in a pinch. The Mariners cut him loose even though he will remain under team control through 2028. Raley's power against righties and an extra year of control could make him a solid bench option moving forward.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Less than 48 hours after telling reporters that Aaron Rodgers was still the Steelers' starting quarterback, Mike McCarthy made the decision to bench the future Hall of Fame quarterback for Friday's game against the Broncos.
    • Recent findings suggest that the Steelers reportedly spent Monday and Tuesday preparing for the Broncos with Rodgers at the helm.
    • Here are the massive questions we have regarding one of the stories of the year in the NFL.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Less than 48 hours after telling reporters that Aaron Rodgers was still the Steelers' starting quarterback, Mike McCarthy made the decision to bench the future Hall of Fame quarterback for Friday's game against the Broncos. Mason Rudolph will start in place of Rodgers, who will be inactive for the game and was reportedly excused from practice Wednesday in light of his benching.

    Recent findings suggest that the Steelers reportedly spent Monday and Tuesday preparing for the Broncos with Rodgers at the helm. That abruptly changed on Tuesday night when McCarthy made the stunning decision following a meeting with other members of Steelers management. Wednesday afternoon saw Rodgers blister McCarthy, who he won a Super Bowl with, in an all-time interview with The Pat McAfee Show.

    Here are the massive questions we have regarding one of the stories of the year in the NFL.

    McCarthy's decision to bench Rodgers was about more than on-field performance.

    Recent findings suggest that ESPN's Ian Rapoport mentioned on The Pat McAfee Show that the decision came down to who's calling plays. The Steelers have been running more hurry-up offense in recent weeks. In those situations, the play-calling runs through Rodgers and quarterbacks coach Tom Arth. McCarthy apparently decided that that was no longer sustainable.

    In a recent development, rodgers himself confirmed on McAfee's show that the decision was partly due to play-calling. Rodgers felt that McCarthy shouldn't call plays and accused McCarthy of being late and sleeping through meetings. Rodgers also said that McCarthy admitted that he hadn't watched film of that week's opponent days leading up to games.

    Rodgers said that he met with McCarthy this week, expressed his concerns and discussed the play-calling duties. Rodgers said that if changes weren't going to be made, he would rather not be the team's quarterback, which is ultimately what happened.

    Industry observers note that the situation with Rodgers had been "brewing for a while" and "reached the point of no return" on Tuesday night, according to longtime Steelers beat reporter Gerry Dulac. The Steelers held a series of internal meetings and conversations over the past two days regarding the offense and what needs to change moving forward, per ESPN. One reported change is a more collaborative approach to play calling, which coincides with Rapoport's report.

    There had been reports of tension between Rodgers and McCarthy. Cameras caught the two exchanging verbal jabs during Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss to Cleveland. There appeared to be a disconnect between the two in recent weeks over the offense from a philosophical standpoint (Rodgers, for example, often checked out of running plays in lieu of passing plays at the line of scrimmage; McCarthy remarked during his Monday presser that the Steelers need to run the ball more).

    It also goes without saying that Rodgers is not playing his best ball in his final NFL season.

    Sources indicate that rodgers, who will turn 43 on Dec. 2, is completing 60.9 percent of his passes this season, the lowest total since his rookie season. During Sunday's loss to the Eagles, Rodgers was sacked five times despite being pressured only eight times. In addition to taking unnecessary sacks, Rodgers missed open receivers multiple times and was inaccurate on several downfield passes.

    Sources indicate that rodgers clearly isn't the only issue. The Steelers' offensive line (which suffered a blow in Week 10 when left guard Mason McCormick suffered an ankle injury that is expected to sideline him for the rest of the regular season) has regressed. Pittsburgh's running game has hit a wall, and the Steelers' receiving corps has underwhelmed, especially DK Metcalf, who was ejected from Sunday's loss in the third quarter after committing his second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty of the half.

    Industry observers note that A breakup probably wasn't going to happen as long as Pittsburgh kept winning. The last two losses were apparently the straws that broke the camel's back.

    Recent findings suggest that in 2023, Rudolph was promoted to starting quarterback following an injury to Kenny Pickett and subpar play from Mitch Trubisky. Rudolph took over with the Steelers sitting at 7-7 (having lost three straight games) and on the precipice of missing the playoffs.

    Rudolph played brilliantly while leading the Steelers to wins over the Bengals and Seahawks and did enough to help the Steelers edge the Ravens in Baltimore in Week 18 to secure a wild card spot in the playoffs.

    Recent findings suggest that A 2018 third-round pick, Rudolph was drafted to potentially serve as Ben Roethlisberger's successor. That never materialized, however, despite Rudolph going 5-3 as Pittsburgh's starter in 2019 after Roethlisberger suffered a season-ending injury. Rudolph was quickly typecast as a game manager and not starter material.

    It has been revealed that mcCarthy, however, spoke glowingly about Rudolph during training camp. At the time, some thought that McCarthy was trying to drum up trade interest in Rudolph. With Tuesday night's announcement, it's clear that McCarthy sees something in Rudolph and wants to give him a chance to run his offense in regular season games.

    Industry observers note that there are reasons to believe that Rudolph will have another successful stint under center for Pittsburgh. The Steelers' remaining schedule includes only two teams with above .500 records. Pittsburgh's defense has been solid this season (they are seventh in the NFL in fewest points allowed) and its receiving corps appears to be getting better. Hurleman caught six passes and a touchdown Sunday in his season debut. Roman Wilson returned from injury last week, and Michael Pittman is expected to play Friday for the first time since Week 4. The Steelers also have one of the league's better running back duos in Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle.

    It has been revealed that the Steelers have two young quarterbacks, Will Howard and Drew Allar, who are under contract. Rudolph, however, is slated to enter free agency this offseason. By making this move, McCarthy is essentially giving Rudolph an audition to be Pittsburgh's quarterback in 2027.

    It has been revealed that if Rudolph plays well and helps lead the Steelers to the playoffs, one would think that the Steelers would re-sign Rudolph this offseason and give him a chance to compete alongside Allar, Howard and whoever the Steelers bring in this offseason. If he doesn't rise to the occasion, the Steelers will likely bring in two quarterbacks this offseason to compete with Howard and Allar.

    According to both sides, yes. Rodgers and McCarthy apparently at odds for months. Rodgers acknowldged on Wednesday that he first noticed McCarthy missing meetings, sleeping, etc. shortly after he signed with the team. The two were seen shouting at each other in Cleveland, which was back in Week 4.

    Rodgers said that his time with the Steelers is over. The Steelers could retain his rights for the rest of the season, or they could release him, which would give him a chance to finish his career somewhere else.

    If he were released, two possible options would be the 49ers and the Packers as a backup to Brock Purdy or Jordan Love. This scenario would give him the opportunity to retire with either his childhood team or the team where he built his NFL legacy. It's also possible that the Patriots and Ravens gives Rodgers a look if he hits the open market.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Last season, the San Francisco 49ers won a close game at the Seattle Seahawks.
    • We have the 49ers' road win over the Seahawks out of the way already this season.
    • The 49ers have been great this season, including a dominant win over the Minnesota Vikings last week.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Last season, the San Francisco 49ers won a close game at the Seattle Seahawks. And then after that the Seahawks became a dominant Super Bowl champion, including two blowout wins of the 49ers.

    We have the 49ers' road win over the Seahawks out of the way already this season. But this season San Francisco is the team that looks like a future Super Bowl champion.

    The 49ers have been great this season, including a dominant win over the Minnesota Vikings last week. The offense has been spectacular. And the defense, ranked seventh in DVOA, has been one of the biggest surprises of the season. That defense has brought the 49ers from being a good team to a potentially great one. Kyle Shanahan, who should be NFL Coach of the Year, was going to field a potent offense. The defense completes the circle.

    However, we can't count out the Seahawks quite yet. The defense has been tremendous again. The offense hasn't been great, but a lot of that is attributed to Sam Darnold playing through injuries almost all season, when he has been able to play. Darnold should return this week, off the Seahawks' bye, and if he's a little healthier and a bit more protective of the ball, Seattle can still play at a high level.

    That's why the Seahawks are not a major underdog this week, even though they play at a 9-1 49ers team. The 49ers are just a 3-point favorite. Not setting the spread above a field goal shows a lot of respect for the reigning champions. But maybe it's not showing enough respect for the 49ers.

    Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers beat the Seahawks 32-29 back in Week 5. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images).

    San Francisco has shown no signs of vulnerability. It had no complications with the Vikings defense, which is the only defense on the same level as Seattle. This looks like a great San Francisco team, and that's why 49ers -3 is the pick. And if the Seahawks can't slow down the 49ers, nobody else in the NFC might be able to do it either.

    Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 12 of the NFL season:.

    It's a little surprising to see Detroit as this major of an underdog. The Lions are 8-2 and very good, especially with the recent defensive improvement. But that defense hasn't faced an offense like Chicago's in a while. The Bears are cooking on offense and defense lately. They haven't even trailed in a game in five weeks. Detroit's defense has been good lately but at some point it seems like injuries to linebacker Jack Campbell and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson will catch up to them, and it could be this week.

    In a recent development, the one dud among the five games between Wednesday and Friday. Here's the conundrum: You can't trust the Cowboys defense to help cover a big spread (even though it did look a little better last week), but you also can't really trust Joe Milton III to help keep the game close. Hopefully the Eagles will be up to playing spoiler for a large audience.

    The biggest factor in this game is whether Buffalo's defensive improvement — the Bills have allowed 37 points in four games — can stick or if it's due to facing a run of bad quarterbacks. If the defensive improvement is legitimate, Buffalo might have its best team of the Josh Allen era. We should find out this week. The Chiefs are very good, too, and in a great matchup it seems smart to grab the three points, though Kenneth Walker III being ruled out makes it a more tepid pick.

    According to recent reports, benching Aaron Rodgers wasn't outlandish after two bad games and a pretty mediocre season. But the way it played out, with it being announced after 11 p.m. on a Tuesday when the Steelers play Friday, was stunning. Now we have to figure out if the Steelers will revolt or rally around Mason Rudolph. This one could get weird, in what is supposed to be rainy weather. The Broncos seem to have found their offensive identity through rookie running back Jonah Coleman, but the Steelers are very good stopping the run. Pittsburgh also should get back to its run game after inexplicably forgetting about it last week, which means Rudolph won't be much of a factor anyway. This has already been a weird week in Pittsburgh.

    PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 22: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers looks on during the game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 22, 2026 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.

    It has been revealed that the Bengals should be upset after losing in the final seconds at Washington on Monday night. And they can take it out on the Saints, who have lost three of four with the only win being when they held off an overtime two-point conversation at home against Shedeur Sanders and the Browns. Joe Burrow should have another monster game.

    Kyle McCord was reasonable in his first start, but that was against the Colts. Last week at Buffalo the Dolphins had what was probably their worst game of the season, and that's saying something for a 1-9 team. The Jets aren't good, but they are coming off a win over the Chargers, and they'll look better when they're playing teams down at their level.

    It has been revealed that the worst thing to happen to Jesse Minter is the defense struggling as badly as it has. If the Ravens were losing because the offense was inept without Lamar Jackson, it would be easy to give him a pass. But Jacoby Brissett has been reasonable and the defense, which is Minter's specialty, has been awful. Baltimore has allowed 32.4 points per game over the past five weeks. The Texans can move the ball and now see an opening for a wild-card spot with the upheaval in Pittsburgh.

    It has been revealed that it's hard to take any underdog lately, with the favorites on a roll the past few weeks. And the Falcons aren't a comfortable underdog to take, but Atlanta has enough talent that it's still the only team to beat the 49ers. The Falcons are coming off a bye, and maybe that helps them keep it close.

    Switching quarterbacks can give a team a short-term boost, especially when that quarterback was the worst in the NFL this season. Daniel Jones wasn't giving the Colts a chance. Anthony Richardson Sr. hasn't been good in the NFL, but he can't be worse than Jones has been. Maybe there's a jolt that gives Indianapolis a chance to keep this one close.

    It would have been nice to see the Titans play better at Dallas last week, but they did end up scoring 30 points. The offense has been decent lately. The problem is the defense, and that's why it's scary to take them even getting more than two touchdowns. But that's a major spread in the NFL.

    Sources indicate that this game could be Tommy DeVito vs. D.J. Uiagalelei, if Justin Herbert doesn't clear concussion protocol. Since there's no reason to rush Herbert back we'll assume he won't play, and then this could turn into one of the ugliest games in the NFL this season.

    Sources indicate that the Cardinals have shown no signs of life lately, after trading Jacoby Brissett, watching Gardner Minshew II go down to injury, losing all their receivers due to injury or trades and then firing their defensive coordinator this week. Whether rookie Carson Beck returns from a back injury or Josh Johnson has to start again, it doesn't really matter. The Commanders aren't great but we can't trust Arizona.

    Fernando Mendoza didn't look bad last week. The Raiders' defense is still terrible and maybe the Browns break out against it, but Cleveland's offense has its challenges too. The Browns play close games, that's what they do, and we'll assume another close one on Sunday night.

    Sources indicate that tampa Bay is getting very little out of Baker Mayfield. But the Buccaneers can still run the ball and play very good defense. A win for Tampa Bay would still leave them at 4-7, but they'd be just a game behind the Panthers for first place and clinch the head-to-head tiebreaker. The first meeting was an absolute blowout, and while that won't repeat, it revealed that Tampa Bay is a hard matchup for Carolina.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The 2026-27 NBA season is barely a month old and trade season won't officially begin until December 15 when players signed this summer are eligible to be moved, but that doesn't stop the rumor machine from churning in the Association.
    • According to recent reports, the first 15 games of the season have been enough for some teams to learn the harsh truth about not being a contender this year, while others are off to surprisingly good starts that could turn them into midseason buyers.
    • The one unknown this season is how the league's lottery reform will affect the in-season trade market.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The 2026-27 NBA season is barely a month old and trade season won't officially begin until December 15 when players signed this summer are eligible to be moved, but that doesn't stop the rumor machine from churning in the Association.

    According to recent reports, the first 15 games of the season have been enough for some teams to learn the harsh truth about not being a contender this year, while others are off to surprisingly good starts that could turn them into midseason buyers. That's how the trade market starts to take shape, and with a trade request already made in Fresh Orleans by Dejounte Murray and a handful of expiring contracts known to be open to moving, we can start piecing together an early look at what trade season may look like.

    The one unknown this season is how the league's lottery reform will affect the in-season trade market. Fewer teams will have incentive to completely bottom out, but even with teams not trying to sell everything off, there will still be enough teams trying to buy to create a market.

    On Thursday, we got a fresh batch of rumors, starting with some updates on potential suitors for Murray after being sent home by the Pelicans.

    Recent findings suggest that murray makes $32.8 million this year and has a player option for $30.8 million next year that he will almost assuredly pick up. That means he's not exactly a coveted asset, and even for teams with a potential need at point guard, so far no one seems to be jumping at the opportunity to trade for the disgruntled Pelicans guard.

    Two teams that were promptly connected as potential destinations for Murray were the Suns and the Heat, both with glaring point guard needs and a desire to contend this season. However, neither team is desperate to make a move right now, according to Jake Fischer in the latest Stein Line newsletter.

    Murray and Klutch Sports see Phoenix as a good landing spot, but the Suns view center as a bigger need than point guard and would demand that the Pelicans send back draft capital to take on Murray's salary, Fischer reports. Miami, meanwhile, has shown little appetite for Murray and he is not expected to be one of its trade targets because of his player option for next season that would severely limit their ability to retool the roster around Giannis Antetokounmpo.

    With the two most obvious potential suitors for Murray not exactly showing a lot of excitement for bringing him in, it seems likely that Murray's trade request and absence from the Pelicans will extend for quite some time and could last all the way to the trade deadline.

    The Washington Wizards are 5-11 to start the season, which makes it increasingly unlikely they will be trying to work out a long-term extension for Davis. The early returns on Washington's commitment to Trae Young have not been good, and if the Wizards are looking to acquire some assets this season, Davis makes the most sense as an expiring contract.

    On the latest episode of the Hoop Collective, ESPN's Brian Windhorst offered an revision on Davis' market and desires for his next contract.

    "I think people have demand for Anthony Davis," Windhorst stated. "They just don't want to give him a max extension, and I don't think he's looking for a max extension, but I do think he's looking for a lot of money.".

    Recent findings suggest that that's not exactly groundbreaking information and any team exploring a trade for Davis will want to know what, exactly, he's looking for in his next contract. Below the max is a start, but teams are growing wary of giving out massive money to aging stars in the second apron era. Davis brings an additional level of risk to any long-term contract discussions with his injury history.

    Recent findings suggest that that stated, he has been quite good this season -- averaging 24.6 points and 10.1 rebounds per game on solid efficiency -- and the Wizards should be shopping him to teams desperate for a center upgrade. If Phoenix is less interested in a point guard but has an appetite for a star center, perhaps the Suns could be a trade partner to offload Jalen Green's contract -- to be clear, that's not a rumor, just connecting dots between a few recent rumors.

    Everything with Davis' market will come down to what Davis and Rich Paul tell teams about what they want his next contract to look like.

    With Murray on the block and the Pelicans at 5-11, it's fair to wonder (again) if some of Upcoming Orleans' more intriguing players could find their way onto the trade market.

    According to recent reports, the player most teams around the league covet in Upcoming Orleans is Trey Murphy III. Even though he's in the midst of a slow start to the season and at the moment dealing with knee tendonitis, other teams still covet his potential as a star on the wing given his abilities as a scorer and defender. The Pelicans also believe strongly in Murphy's upside, and unfortunately for other teams, Fischer reports Murphy -- unlike Murray -- has no desire to make a trade request.

    Sources indicate that as such, he's going to be quite expensive to pry from the Pelicans, who "remain reluctant" to discuss trades for Murphy. Given he's their best potential trade chip, that's probably a wise approach, and Newly introduced Orleans will hope some hopeful contender is desperate enough to give up a haul of assets before they consider moving him.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples.

    Thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Saturday's supply just below.

    Will the San Francisco Giants trade their ace this offseason? That's a reasonable question to ask now that FanSided is reporting that the Giants are open to trade discussions regarding veteran right-hander Logan Webb. No doubt, Webb would be a coveted presence on the offseason market.

    Industry observers note that webb, who just recently turned 30, endured a bit of a down 2026 on the run-prevention front, but the overall body of work remains very strong. For his career, the three-time All-Star has a career ERA+ of 115 with three top-10 finishes in the American League Cy Young vote. In three of the past four seasons, he's topped 200 innings.

    Webb is under contract through 2028, and that extra year of team control makes him even more of an alluring trade target for contenders in need of rotation upgrades.

    Freddy Peralta, who'll be going into his age-31 season in 2027, is one of the strongest free-agent starting pitchers on the market not named Tarik Skubal. As such, there's healthy interest in his services. The Tampa Bay Rays, the Chicago White Sox, the San Diego Padres, the Toronto Blue Jays, and two presently unknown clubs all have significant interest in signing Peralta, the Athletic reports.

    Peralta, coming off three straight seasons for the Milwaukee Brewers in which he topped 30 starts and 200 strikeouts, wasn't himself with the Fresh York Mets for the first half-plus of 2027. However, after a deadline trade to the Rays, he made some adjustments and re-established himself as a highly useful starter. The market's going to reflect his rediscovered form.

    Recent findings suggest that right-hander Hiromi Itoh, who's seeking to make the leap from Japan to MLB, was recently in Chicago to visit the Cubs or the White Sox, ESPN reports. Both Windy City squads are in need of pitching help, and Itoh would certainly help them on that front.

    According to recent reports, the 29-year-old Itoh ranked 26th on CBS Sports' offseason list of the top free agents in the current class. Here's part of our write-up:.

    It has been revealed that "A down 2026 season took some of the shine off Itoh, who won the 2025 Eiji Sawamura Award (Japan's Cy Young equivalent) after throwing 196 ⅔ innings with a 2.52 ERA. To be sure, Itoh pitched well in 2026 (3.18 ERA in 172 ⅔ innings), but he was not as consistently dominant as in the past. The 5-foot-9 right-hander is a seven-pitch pitcher with a low-90s fastball and the usual array of secondary pitches (sinker, cutter, curveball, slider, sweeper, splitter), none of which stands out as a plus offering. Itoh has thrown at least 150 innings in each of the last six seasons. He's seen as a crafty back-end starter in MLB, or perhaps even a reliever (Itoh sat 96 mph out of the bullpen in the World Baseball Classic). The Hokkaido Nippon Ham Fighters are expected to post Itoh, who turned 29 in August, this winter.".

    The Cubs have a lot of uncertainty in the rotation, while the White Sox still need help even after adding Dustin May this offseason.

    The Latest York Mets retained the services of first baseman Mark Vientos leading up to the recent non-tender deadline despite his pattern of decline over the last two seasons. Now, Vientos could be on the move. The soon-to-be 27-year-old has been the subject of trade inquiries, The Athletic reports.

    Sources indicate that while Vientos is coming off a highly disappointing 2026 season, he still has power potential and in his semi-recent past a 2024 campaign in which he hit 27 home runs in 111 games. All of that makes Vientos a fairly compelling change-of-scenery possibility, and the Mets may seek to make that happen this winter.

    Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

    📅 31 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1119 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • In a recent development, kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    In a recent development, kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    According to recent reports, kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    In a recent development, it's vital to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    Industry observers note that right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    We already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    It has been revealed that however, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't at the moment have on their roster.

    Industry observers note that carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    In a recent development, similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    Industry observers note that utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    Sources indicate that allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

    Aaron Rodgers' brother has a theory on why QB was shockingly benched by Steelers

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (812 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Pittsburgh Steelers made one of the most shocking moves of the NFL season on Tuesday night when they decided to bench Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph for Friday's game against the Broncos.
    • According to recent reports, when the announcement came out at 11:10 p.m.
    • The younger Rodgers brother believes that Steelers general manager Omar Khan may have played a part in the decision.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Pittsburgh Steelers made one of the most shocking moves of the NFL season on Tuesday night when they decided to bench Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph for Friday's game against the Broncos.

    According to recent reports, when the announcement came out at 11:10 p.m. ET, the Steelers didn't offer any reason for the benching, but one person close to Rodgers has a theory on why the QB was benched and that's his brother, Jordan Rodgers.

    The younger Rodgers brother believes that Steelers general manager Omar Khan may have played a part in the decision. With the Steelers playing on Friday this week, they held a practice on Tuesday and Aaron took all of the first team reps during that session, which made the decision to bench him so bizarre.

    Jordan thinks Steelers general manager Omar Khan may have played a part in decision to bench his brother.

    "Remember, yesterday was not a normal Tuesday," Jordan stated on Wednesday's edition of ESPN's Get Up. "So there was a practice yesterday where presumably Aaron was the starter for the entire practice, so something had to happen. Him and Mike [McCarthy] have been together so long, the conversations have spanned every aspect of what you could with a head coach and a quarterback, so I don't think that was the problem. To me, this has to be a Omar Khan thing.".

    It's certainly an interesting theory. As Jordan noted, Aaron spent 13.5 seasons with McCarthy, so the two of them have been through some battles together. Also, McCarthy had declared Rodgers as his starter on Monday when he was asked if there was any thought about benching his quarterback.

    As for Khan, Rodgers did seem to take a subtle shot at the front office over the handling of Max Hurleman. The Steelers QB is a big fan of the second-year receiver and he made it clear that he was not happy about the fact that Hurleman didn't get a chance to play until Week 11 (The receiver spent the first 10 weeks of the season on the practice squad).

    Hurleman ended up being one of the few bright spots for the Steelers in their 19-16 loss to the Eagles, leading the team with six receptions for 61 yards and his first career touchdown.

    According to recent reports, "I think it's as much for him as it is for everybody else upstairs making decisions. You know, I think everyone thought before the injury in camp that he was a 53 (roster) guy," Rodgers noted of Hurleman. "I know the guys in our room did for sure. So for him to go out there and finally get elevated and go out and play the way he played was not surprising to any of us but great for his confidence and a great reminder for the folks upstairs what kind of player he is.".

    Aaron was presumably referring to Khan and the Steelers' front office when he mentioned the "Folks upstairs.".

    It's unclear whether Khan had anything to do with the decision to bench Aaron, but, either way, he deserved much of the blame for how the season is going, according to Jordan.

    According to recent reports, "This season, the lack of success, to me, is more of an indictment on Omar Khan and how he constructed this roster because they're in the middle of the last dance and rebuild," Jordan said. "And it was a bad combination to be in that spot, but you trade away arguably your two best players in George Pickens and then Joey Porter Jr. on the other side. You got a draft pick in the fourth round as a kick returner (Kaden Wetjen) that can't even return kicks anymore that can't impact the Steelers wide receiver room, there's problems everywhere. So to me, Mason's not solving that this week.".

    Jordan also said that if you're going to bench Aaron, it doesn't make much sense to give the job to Rudolph.

    "I look at this roster and I go, I would've been less surprised waking up hearing Will Howard or Drew Allar was the starter," Jordan said. "If you need a quarterback that's a little younger, that can move around a little bit more, or you're looking to the future, that would make more sense, but their lack of success this year -- and Aaron hasn't played great the last couple weeks -- but there was also a month ago when we're saying, 'He looks like vintage. He's moving around better. He's got three touchdowns in a row for three weeks in a row.'".

    Jordan had actually been estranged from Aaron for several years, but at some point over the past few months, the two made up, with Aaron even visiting Jordan last week while his younger brother was working a game as an ESPN announcer.
