    #199425. Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1438 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1438 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • They will consider almost any path to improving their rosters, no matter how obscure or unexpected.
    • Recent findings suggest that on Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common.
    • So, let's consider this rumor in earnest.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    NBA teams are remarkably diligent. They will consider almost any path to improving their rosters, no matter how obscure or unexpected. Still, every now and then, a truly bizarre nugget hits the rumor mill and forces us to consider what exactly a team is thinking.

    Recent findings suggest that on Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common. Teams will do due diligence on a wide variety of players leading up to transaction periods in order to make sure they've covered their bases, and Begley gives no indication that there have even been talks between the Jazz and the Dallas Mavericks. Still, as he notes, "you're not gonna spend a lot of time on a player if you don't have any interest in him, so the idea of Utah spending some time internally on Kyrie Irving was interesting.".

    So, let's consider this rumor in earnest. The Jazz entered this season with playoff expectations after four straight years in the lottery. They are 3-13 due to a combination of injuries, players adjusting to a fresh roster and simply poor performance. Utah has shown a willingness to trade for players outside of its perceived timeline before. The Jazz looked at then-33-year-old Jrue Holiday early in their rebuild in 2023, for instance, but backed off when Holiday's camp reportedly made it clear he would not be interested in extending.

    According to recent reports, irving, still a star-caliber scorer, has the Mavericks at 8-7 through 15 games. He's averaging over 22 points on roughly his standard efficiency for a Dallas team with pretty limited shooting around him. We can't say at this stage whether or not the Mavericks are willing to trade him. The notion that they might depends on the team's asset deficit (Dallas does not control its own first-round pick again until 2031) and the 15-year age gap between Irving and franchise player Cooper Flagg, but Dallas could easily elect to simply build off this early success.

    In a recent development, if they do take the long view and consider trade offers, Irving could absolutely help a team trying to win right now. Plenty of teams potentially looking for individual shot-creation, like the Detroit Pistons, Houston Rockets and Miami Heat, could be planning pursuits of the future Hall of Famer.

    The question here is why the Jazz, specifically, would be interested in Irving, because on paper, there is perhaps not a single, high-profile player who makes less sense for this roster than he does. Utah's young core revolves around three perimeter players: Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey. The Jazz are so strong on that front that Bailey came off the bench to start the season, and it's unclear how exactly they plan to handle their starting five when Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. return from injuries. If Utah isn't comfortable with Jackson playing center full time, and the Memphis Grizzlies certainly weren't, then one of those five players either needs to get traded or come off the bench.

    Adding Irving to this logjam doesn't make sense. Neither does trading one of those players for Irving. George is 23. Bailey is 20. Peterson is 19. Teams that are 10 games below .500 simply don't trade foundational pieces for players a decade or more their senior. They gave up three first-round picks for Jackson largely to improve their defense, and now that Walker Kessler plays for the Los Angeles Lakers, his presence matters more than ever.

    Markkanen is the obvious trade candidate of the group, but he's still five years younger than Irving and plays a less saturated position. If Utah viewed Markkanen's max contract as a negative it needed to escape, that would be one thing, but there's just no evidence at this stage that this is the case. They have rebuffed trade interest in Markkanen at every turn. If Dallas were willing to put substantial draft equity on the table to cover the age and positional gaps here, there could perhaps be a conversation, but Dallas isn't in a position to do so.

    According to recent reports, there's some merit to the idea that Utah might eventually want to shake up its backcourt. There were rumors during the draft process that Peterson's representatives were skeptical of Utah as a landing spot because they also represent George and felt that two score-first guards would clash. Even if the Jazz were prepared to split them up less than 20 games into Peterson's career, Irving himself has typically fared far better when he has been paired with a high-level passer. He won his championship with LeBron James. He's thriving next to Cooper Flagg now. His best trait is, and always has been, his scoring.

    And then, of course, there is the history shared between Irving and Utah's top executive. The CEO of the Jazz is Danny Ainge, who once traded for Irving when he ran the Boston Celtics. Before his second season in Boston, Irving publicly shared looks to re-sign with the Celtics as a free agent in 2019. When the time came, he instead joined the Brooklyn Nets, a divisional opponent. This is the NBA. If LeBron James can reunite with Dan Gilbert, any player-executive reunion is theoretically possible. Nonetheless, Ainge and Irving would seemingly be among the unlikeliest pairings in all of basketball. Put all of this together and this is a puzzling rumor to say the least.

    In a recent development, sometimes a rumor says more about a team's significant-picture plans than it does a specific target. For a variety of reasons, some of which we've covered, it seems exceedingly unlikely that the Jazz are going to trade for Irving. However, they've invested the time in considering it, as Begley noted. That means something, even if it doesn't mean a trade is coming.

    In a recent development, the simplest read on this is that Utah is concerned enough about its short-term prospects that it is considering investing in win-now help despite its 3-13 start. That, in itself, makes sense. The Jazz don't control their own first-round pick this season. They have no incentive to lose, and while making the postseason despite starting the season 10 games under .500 is improbable, it just happened a year ago when the 4-14 Charlotte Hornets recovered promptly enough to reach the Play-In Tournament. The Jazz are 5.5 games out of the No. 10 seed in the Western Conference right now. If they get healthy in time and make the right addition, perhaps they could still make a real run at it.

    Recent findings suggest that skepticism about the George-Peterson fit, for now, should be on the back burner. Though the two fared far better early on when they played separately, both, at least for now, have better net ratings and true shooting percentages in the minutes they've shared than the minutes they haven't. George's usage skyrockets when he plays without Peterson, but that's to be expected with Markkanen and Jackson out.

    Recent findings suggest that there may have been concern early in the season, and that might have been when Irving crossed Utah's mind. There may still be concerns down the line when the Jazz have had a longer sample size to evaluate the pairing with the rest of their roster. For now, though, it's simply too early to consider splitting up such a talented tandem, especially right as the team has actually started winning some games.

    Industry observers note that however, ball-handling behind them is a valid concern. Utah declined its fourth-year option on backup point guard and former first-round pick Isaiah Collier, and the offense has been 6.5 points per 100 possessions worse with him on the floor this season. Adding a veteran backup point guard, if only to ease Peterson's burden during the minutes George rests, would be sensible. Irving is obviously no backup, but as perhaps the most notable point guard theoretically on the market, it makes sense that the Jazz would at least broach the concept internally.

    Sources indicate that ainge hasn't earned the nickname "Trader Danny" for nothing. His teams are almost always at the center of the trade market, and as last year's Jackson deal proved, he's as capable of a stunner as he's ever been. Irving would certainly qualify as one. We shouldn't expect it. It wouldn't really make sense based on what we know now. But in the post-Luka Dončić trade NBA, it would be hard to dismiss basically any rumor involving a player of this stature.

    • Which teams might make for a good fit for Webb?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Coming off a disaster of a season and with a roster badly in need of an overhaul, the Giants make sense as a team to make a trade or two this offseason. Sure enough, they are "listening to trade offers" for All-Star starting pitcher Logan Webb, per The Athletic, but they'd need a "very strong return" in order to deal him.

    Recent findings suggest that webb, 30, has two years and $47 million left on his current deal. He went 8-9 with a 4.31 ERA and 1.3 WAR last season, but it was his worst year in quite a while. He averaged 4.5 WAR per season in the previous four years with a 3.22 ERA and led the National League in innings pitched from 2023 to 2025, racking up three straight top-six Cy Young finishes.

    Which teams might make for a good fit for Webb? Many of them. We're talking about a workhorse under team control for two more years. Let's run through five of the best fits while, again, knowing that basically any contender should be interested in at least a conversation with the Giants.

    The Cubs need so much pitching this offseason. Their entire rotation heading into the playoffs last season is in free agency. This isn't hyperbole. Matthew Boyd, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes and David Peterson are all off the roster. If the Cubs were to try and put together a rotation right now, it would be something like Justin Steele, Edward Cabrera, Javier Assad and several question marks. Ben Brown and Cade Horton will open the season on the injured list.

    According to recent reports, do we really need to spell out what a reliable innings eater would mean for this bunch? Webb is an outstanding fit here.

    Sources indicate that the upstart playoff team last season was a ton of fun, but also was running bullpen games in the ALDS. The White Sox just attached Davis Martin to Luis Castillo in a trade to the Rockies in order to offload Castillo's contract, too, so they're down a starter. The Dustin May signing means they have him along with Sean Burke and converted reliever Grant Taylor. The White Sox would reportedly like to sign another starter in the May ballpark, but what about trading for someone better like Webb?

    A top four in the rotation of Webb, Burke, Taylor and May would be exponentially better than what the Sox had last season.

    Returns of Spencer Strider and Spencer Schwellenbach at some point will help, but this is still a thin rotation for a team coming off a division title. Chris Sale remains, but he's followed up with Grant Holmes and Bryce Elder before the Spencers return. Youngster Didier Fuentes moving to the rotation is exciting, but there are an awful lot of questions behind Sale, who turns 38 in late March, by the way.

    Given that the Padres reside in the NL West with the Giants, there might be a bit of an intradivision tax in terms of the asking price, but Padres boss A.J. Preller is never shy about offloading prospects. There could certainly be a fit. The Padres need rotation help, too, after losing Michael King, Nick Pivetta, Robbie Ray and others to free agency. We know they're in on Tarik Skubal, but that doesn't mean they'll be content with just landing one significant fish.

    Look at the current Padres rotation. It's basically Joe Musgrove and Randy Vásquez. With three straight playoff berths and zero trips to the World Series, now isn't the time to have Jhony Brito, Ryan Weiss and Ian Koenig make up 60% of the rotation.

    Dealing for Webb and signing Skubal would make for a nice offseason for fresh ownership, no?

    One of the most disappointing teams in baseball last season needs to have a prolific offseason. We've heard plenty about the Mets being involved in the Skubal sweepstakes and we've seen them win a monster bidding war before (see: Soto, Juan). Grabbing Webb would make it quite a well-rounded rotation with talented youngsters Nolan McLean, Christian Scott and Zac Thornton.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the NFL on Wednesday will debut the first Thanksgiving Eve game in league history, and it could feature the return of a superstar defender.
    • Recent findings suggest that "I would say I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday, but for sure this season," Parsons said on Monday.
    • The Packers could use a lift as they gear up for a run at the NFC North title.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the NFL on Wednesday will debut the first Thanksgiving Eve game in league history, and it could feature the return of a superstar defender. Green Bay Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons is active for the first time this season and cleared to make his first appearance of the year in the contest against the Los Angeles Rams, but it remains unclear whether he will play. Regardless of when it occurs, the All-Pro will soon enter game action for the first time since he tore his ACL and meniscus last year.

    Recent findings suggest that "I would say I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday, but for sure this season," Parsons said on Monday. "And I'll be looking forward to returning to the field.".

    The Packers could use a lift as they gear up for a run at the NFC North title. If Parsons suits up this week, he could wreak havoc on an injury-riddled Rams offense and guide Green Bay to one of its biggest wins of the year to begin the regular season's final push.

    In a recent development, the Kansas City Chiefs were seeking a similar boost from their top running back, Kenneth Walker III, who missed the last two games with a groin injury. As a contender for the league lead in rushing yards per game, Walker has been instrumental in the Chiefs' offensive resurgence in 2026, and the unit will need to fire on all cylinders to keep up with the Buffalo Bills in one of the NFL's biggest blockbuster battles of the year.

    Walker returned to practice on Tuesday as a limited participant, but the Chiefs are ruling him out for the holiday showdown.

    Below is the latest on all the other injuries that could impact the NFL's Thanksgiving and Thanksgiving Eve slate.

    Parsons' potential insertion into Wednesday's lineup would be a boon to the Packers, who in their last outing surrendered 30 points to the typically silent Minnesota Vikings offense. It would also inject life into a roster that will again be without another of its stars, Josh Jacobs. Green Bay's top running back continues to nurse the finger injury he sustained in Week 9, which required surgery. With Jacobs ruled out for the second consecutive game, the rushing attack could remain a non-factor. The run game is historically bleak, as its 3.1 yards per game is on pace to be the worst by any NFL team since 2000.

    The Los Angeles Rams' injured reserve remains loaded with impactful pass-catchers. Last week, the team ruled superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua out for the season. This week, it was determined that Davante Adams will not return from a torn hamstring for at least another game and that tight end Terrance Ferguson is out for the year. Ferguson will undergo surgery on the injured ankle that put him on the shelf nearly two months ago. None of those three played in the Rams' 34-6 demolition of the Arizona Cardinals, but the caliber of opponent increases significantly on Wednesday, so the hampered passing attack might not be nearly as impactful this time out.

    The Chicago Bears defensive backfield depth took a hit over the last two weeks. Kyler Gordon has not played since Nov. 8 and is trending toward another absence, which leaves open a hole at the starting slot cornerback spot, and backup safety Elijah Hicks entered concussion protocol on Tuesday and was promptly ruled out for the Thanksgiving clash with the Detroit Lions. Chicago's running back rotation is also in flux after Roschon Johnson was carted off the field last week. He is third in line for carries behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, but with the latter playing through turf toe, his presence has become more important of late.

    An already banged-up defensive line in Detroit is in even worse shape coming out of the win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. In the wake of Aidan Hutchinson's torn ACL, the Lions also lost rookie Skyler Gill-Howard for the season, as coach Dan Campbell declared on Tuesday that the defensive tackle will undergo surgery on his knee. And on the edge, DJ Wonnum became all the more important in Hutchinson's absence and is now in danger of missing time himself with the back injury that popped up against the Buccaneers. Campbell stated that all players listed on the injury report outside of Gill-Howard will be game-time decisions.

    Saquon Barkley departed from last week's win with his second stinger of the season and remarked after the game that he does not expect to be at full strength for the remainder of the season due to multiple lingering concerns. His status for Week 12 was initially up in the air when the Philadelphia Eagles estimated him as a non-participant on Monday, but he practiced in full on Tuesday and should be good to go for the rivalry clash with the Dallas Cowboys. Another positive development was Quinyon Mitchell's return to practice after he missed Week 11 and was listed as a Monday non-participant.

    It has been revealed that the Cowboys had no trouble moving the ball without Tyler Booker and Jake Ferguson last week and might have to operate without the starting guard and tight end again on Thursday since neither has been able to practice. The beleaguered Dallas defense, on the other hand, could get two linebackers into action with Jaishawn Barham and Dee Winters both progressing from estimated non-participation to limited participation on Tuesday. The former did not play against the Tennessee Titans, and the latter left that game with a knee contusion.

    Sources indicate that if Walker can play in the Thanksgiving finale, the Chiefs will be loaded at running back since Emmett Johnson starred in his absence as a premier rookie ball carrier. Whoever operates in the run game could be without one starting blocker, though, as right tackle Jaylon Moore still has not practiced since he sustained an ankle injury in Week 9. On the other side of the trenches, Omarr Norman-Lott is close to his season debut after the Chiefs activated him from the reserve/PUP list last week.

    Most of the players listed on the Buffalo Bills' injury report sustained their ailments in Week 10 against the Fresh York Jets. Christian Benford, Dalton Kincaid, T.J. Sanders and Dorian Williams all missed last week's matchup with the Miami Dolphins as a result of their injuries. It is a positive sign to see all of them practice in at least a limited capacity, but Sanders missed the entire previous week. O'Cyrus Torrence's ankle problem would be a significant one if it keeps him out of action against the Chiefs, because the right guard has not missed a game since he was drafted in 2023.

    Welcome to Thanksgiving week. Here in Major League Baseball news, that normally means we're bound for a slow week -- save for a few notable exceptions -- but with the CBA expiring on Dec. 1, we might just be in for a free agent frenzy. Let's hope that's the case.

    We can start today's set of news and rumors with the biggest free agent out there.

    It has been revealed that tarik Skubal is the No. 1 free agent this offseason and the two-time Cy Young winner appears on pace to make a decision before the CBA expires. Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, hit MLB Network Radio on Sunday and said that there's a "strong likelihood" that a decision comes by that Dec. 1 deadline, especially given that Skubal's signing impacts so many other pitchers (Boras mentioned that it impacts "10-15 pitchers").

    The 30-year-old lefty was 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158 ⅔ innings last season, as he bounced back after just six weeks from elbow surgery.

    The teams most heavily involved in the Skubal rumors to this point have been the Dodgers, Mets, Padres and Blue Jays, all of whom had in-person meetings with him last week.

    The Tigers have agreed to a deal with right-hander Luis Gil, per ESPN. It's a one-year, $2.3 million deal.

    In a recent development, gil won the American League Rookie of the Year after a productive 2024 season in which he won 15 games and had a 3.50 ERA, but he spent a good portion of 2026 in the minors and was nontendered by the Yankees on Friday. In his limited MLB time last season, Gil had a 4.61 ERA, 1.43 WHIP and 17 strikeouts in 27 ⅓ innings.

    The Tigers rotation seems set with Framber Valdez, Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan, so consider Gil a depth option.

    The Red Sox also reportedly demonstrated interest.

    Tarik Skubal signing with Mets: Two-time Cy Young winner lands historic nine-year, $450 million contract

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (734 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, ace left-hander Tarik Skubal, winner of the last two American League Cy Young awards and far and away the top free agent of the 2026-27 class, has agreed to terms with the New York Mets on a nine-year contract worth $450 million, reports the New York Post.
    • Once finalized, the deal will make Skubal the highest-paid pitcher in Major League Baseball history, in terms of both total contract value and average annual salary.
    • Skubal, who turned 30 years of age on Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, ace left-hander Tarik Skubal, winner of the last two American League Cy Young awards and far and away the top free agent of the 2026-27 class, has agreed to terms with the New York Mets on a nine-year contract worth $450 million, reports the New York Post. The deal has a $45 million signing bonus with no options or opt-outs, per SNY, as well as a full no-trade clause, so the Mets have locked Skubal up for the full nine years. Further, there are only $30 million in deferrals, according to the New York Post. The deal is pending a physical.

    Once finalized, the deal will make Skubal the highest-paid pitcher in Major League Baseball history, in terms of both total contract value and average annual salary.

    Skubal, who turned 30 years of age on Nov. 20, is the No. 1 ranked talent on our list of the top 50 free agents for this offseason. Here's part of Mike Axisa's write-up:.

    Sources indicate that "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He showed few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    Over the last three seasons, Skubal has pitched to a 2.42 ERA and an FIP of 2.48 in 546 innings spread over 88 starts. That amounts to a total WAR of 17.7 since the start of the 2024 campaign. Skubal remains foremost in the discussion for best pitcher in baseball, and this signing reflects that reality.

    Recent findings suggest that since Skubal was traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the 2026 deadline, he was ineligible to receive the qualifying offer from the Dodgers. As such, the Mets will not be penalized a draft pick for signing Skubal.

    The nine years here aren't record-setting, as the longest pitcher contract remains the 12-year deal that Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers. Yamamoto's $325 million was previously the largest contract for a pitcher -- obviously excepting Shohei Ohtani, as he's a two-way player -- so Skubal's $450 million shatters that record.

    Industry observers note that coming off a disappointing 88-loss campaign in 2026, the Mets, substantial-spending owner Steve Cohen, and lead decision-maker David Stearns needed to make an offseason splash to improve their chances of a 2027 rebound and inspire a perhaps disaffected fan base. Skubal more than qualifies. He'll front a Mets rotation that also includes 25-year-old right-hander Nolan McLean, who himself has frontline long-term potential. In Queens, Skubal joins a roster that also includes the All-Star likes of Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor, and Bo Bichette.

    Further, the Mets just locked up young outfielder A.J. Ewing to an eight-year, $95 million extension and we all know plenty about Soto's monster contract. The Mets now have Soto through 2039, Skubal through 2035, Ewing through 2034 and Lindor through 2031.

    The rotation for the Mets right now looks something like:.

    According to recent reports, given the large outlay for Skubal here, the Mets should be all-in on improving the ballclub for the 2027 season, which means we shouldn't expect them to stop with just signing Skubal. That last spot in the rotation, as such, should be ticketed to someone else outside the organization at present, whether a free agent or a trade acquisition.

    The landing of the top free agent available no doubt ramps up the pressure on Stearns and the Mets to deliver a playoff berth and a deep October run in 2027, but Skubal's presence also makes it much likely that such a feat comes to pass.

    #199415. NFL on Thanksgiving cheat sheet: Everything you need to know to impress relatives during three holiday games

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1898 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    NFL on Thanksgiving cheat sheet: Everything you need to know to impress relatives during three holiday games

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that thanksgiving is finally here, and that means the family gets to gather around the table and share one thing we all know and love …football games with stakes!
    • According to recent reports, in this game between two divisional heavyweights, we're going to focus on the trenches when the Lions have the ball.
    • Take this play against the Saints as an example.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that thanksgiving is finally here, and that means the family gets to gather around the table and share one thing we all know and love …football games with stakes! If we include the Thanksgiving Eve game between the Packers and Rams and the Black Friday game between the Steelers and Broncos, all five Thanksgiving Eve/Day/Black Friday games have major implications for both the AFC and NFC playoff races. Some of the league's best are playing on Turkey Day, so just for you, I've put together a special Thanksgiving plate of matchups to watch for on Thanksgiving Day. Let's hop in and establish some fun!

    According to recent reports, in this game between two divisional heavyweights, we're going to focus on the trenches when the Lions have the ball. Since adding DT Jeffrey Simmons, the Bears' defense has taken a major leap in efficiency. According to TruMedia, the Bears have the 4th-best Defensive EPA per play and Defensive Success Rate since Week 8, and a large part of that is Jeffrey Simmons lifting the Bears' defense to new heights. What's really stood out is that with Simmons on the field, Bears' defensive coordinator Dennis Allen can really unlock his Rolodex of coverages on 3rd down without resorting to blitzing as much. Before Simmons came around, the Bears had a 39.3% blitz rate on 3rd down, and when they didn't blitz, their 43.2% pressure rate was 15th in the NFL. Since adding Simmons, their blitz rate on third down has dropped to 25.7%, while their pressure rate without blitzing has risen to 46.2%. With Simmons on the field, Allen can use those blitz looks to scheme up 1v1 chances for Simmons, or force teams to show attention to him that frees up his teammates.

    Take this play against the Saints as an example. It's 3rd and 4, and the Bears line up in a BOSS (Big On Same Side) front, meaning three of their defensive linemen (including Simmons) are lined up on the defense's right, and LB TJ Edwards is lined up over the right guard. In this moment, the Saints are forced to slide the protection to the three defensive linemen and leave the right guard to block Edwards. At the snap, Allen changes the picture, dropping Edwards and giving Simmons a 1v1. Simmons wins instantly and forces Shough out of the pocket and into a pass short of the sticks.

    This will be Simmons and the Bears' biggest test since the trade, as they face a Lions offense that has been hitting all the right notes. Since their last loss in week four, the Lions are fourth in the NFL in Offensive Success Rate, fifth in EPA per play and fifth in points per drive. Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing has done a really good job of mixing in his own unique flavors to the Detroit offense, but what I really think has helped the most is the offensive line stability and growth. Penei Sewell has fully settled in at left tackle, Christian Mahogany has taken back over at left guard after a suspension and center Juice Scruggs has rebounded from his rough play early in the season to provide stability after starter Cade Mays got hurt. Petzing has gotten creative with his pass protection around Goff (see: the Minnesota game), but the step up in pass pro is due to the overall quality of the OL and some impressive blocks by Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki.

    Industry observers note that against the Bucs, Goff and the Lions absolutely ripped passes down the seams of the defense, and the pass protection did their job to let those chunk plays happen. This one is a five-out play, where all five eligible receivers are out into the passing concept if Vaki doesn't get a blitzer. Look at how pristine this pocket is. Mahogany takes his man and deposits him across the formation as well.

    This game is going to be all about trench warfare, as the good Lord intended. There's definitely going to be a lot of points, but when you watch this game as you sit down for your first plate of food, keep an eye on the offensive line for the Lions as they try to handle the Jeffrey Simmons problem.

    According to recent reports, this one doesn't quite have the same juice we might've thought it would coming into the season — it doesn't even have the same juice we thought it would a month ago. But it's a rivalry game nonetheless, and for the Cowboys it's a chance to stay alive in their hopes of winning the division. These teams have played before this season, and while some of the faces might look different, the objective for Dallas remains the same:.

    "Run the ball." - Georgia Tech head coach Brent Keypic.twitter.com/yFuipSdv3a.

    Since the win against the Eagles, the Cowboys have run for over 100 yards twice in four games, and since Week 8 Dallas is fifth in EPA per designed rushing attempt (which excludes scrambles) and rushing Success Rate. Part of this emergence has been the offensive line play, which came into the season as a strength and has weathered injuries to get better at the right time. But the other part of it is Brian Schottenheimer getting a little more creative with his run schemes. Through the first seven weeks of the season, Dallas felt like their offense was static. Since Week 8, their motion rate at the snap has ticked up, and it especially has jumped up in the run game. The motion usage and creativity were on display when Kavontae Turpin ran in a 22-yard touchdown against the Titans. Turpin is lined up in the backfield, and the RB goes in orbit motion around him. Then, Dallas runs pin and pull to get their linemen in space against cornerbacks. Advantage: Dallas.

    Industry observers note that tyler Guyton, Tyler Smith and Cooper Beebe all had killer blocks on this Turpin TD run off pin n pull. #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/9HTr0OqWoR.

    Philadelphia is coming off one of their best performances against the run, holding the Steelers to their lowest success rate on designed carries since the first game of the season. What was most impressive about the performance was their tackling, especially by the linebacker group. Pittsburgh's offense relies heavily on yards after the catch and yards after contact, and in their game against the Eagles, they only had one tackle avoided on rushing attempts and 1.80 yards after contact per carry. The Eagles rely heavily on their linebackers to flow fast to the ball in the run game; living in light run boxes requires your linebackers to be real players.

    Outside of Zack Baun, it hasn't always been perfect, but LB Jeremiah Trotter Jr. might've played one of his best career games. He was decisive and fast, filling the run and making a bunch of splash plays in space.

    Heck of a game for Jeremiah Trotter Jr. Sure helps when the #Steelers don't block you on half their runs.Reminds me of another #54. Fred Warner in the '23 opener when he dominated all game. Ground game doesn't stand a chance with LBs running free. pic.twitter.com/U7H2gPQaZZ.

    Second-year LB Jihaad Campbell hasn't been as consistent, but even he had his flashes on Sunday. If you're looking to watch something, anything during this game, look at how the Cowboys run the ball against an Eagles front coming off a really good performance.

    The nightcap might be the most anticipated game of the Thanksgiving Day festivities, as we get another battle between two of the best QBs of the 2020s. Kansas City heads to Buffalo in a game that could also decide home-field advantage in the AFC. The biggest matchup is obviously going to be which defense can slow down the opposing QB, but for this one I'm choosing to focus on the Bills' defense, which is playing sound football, going up against a now-multifaceted Kansas City offense.

    In a recent development, very slowly, the Chiefs' passing game has rounded into form since their week seven debacle against the Seahawks. Since Week 8, the Chiefs are fifth in the NFL in Success Rate and fourth in the NFL in EPA per play, but if you just take their passing offense since adding WR Josh Downs, the number goes to a 52.6% Passing Success Rate and their EPA per pass has jumped up from 0.17 to 0.22. What Downs has given the Chiefs is another savvy route runner who easily finds holes in zones and creates separation when the Chiefs need him to. Downs is third on the Chiefs in targets since being traded to Kansas City, and you can feel his presence on the field when finding holes in zones.

    This was a fun play for Downs that highlights his ability to find holes in zone coverage and make himself available. The Cardinals are running Cover 6, with the Cover 2 corner to Downs' side. Kansas City is running a Sail concept, with Downs running the "sail" part of the route. Instead of running into the coverage, Downs sits and finds the hole between the two defenders as the go route clears the outside cornerback. Results in an easy first down for the Chiefs.

    3rd and Josh Downs, this time in KC. Downs made a couple of these plays, out routes settling into holes of zones from the slot. He and the emergence of Cyrus Allen have given the Chiefs offense more layers pic.twitter.com/rzk4xinRFH.

    Industry observers note that on the flip side, the Bills' defense hasn't allowed a touchdown on 43 straight possessions, one shy of an NFL record set in 2019 by the Newly introduced England Patriots. Yes, the offenses they've played haven't been super impressive, but what they've done to get their secondary turned around is pretty notable. Through the first seven weeks, the Bills were a Cover 3 and Quarters team, asking their DBs to match and communicate as routes were being passed off. Since week 8, they've played much more Cover 2 as their changeup to Cover 3, meaning fewer guys have to run and match and more guys using physicality at the line of scrimmage and driving on routes quickly.

    Industry observers note that I think this fits more of the personnel that the Bills have. I've always loved CB Christian Benford in more of a physical, press alignment to get eyes and hands on the receiver, and rookie CB Davison Igbinosun is tailor-made for that style of football. The trade for S Amani Hooker gives them a playmaker on the back end, and everything is tied together much more. Again, this is against the Dolphins, but this is good work by the Bills, rotating into an inverted Cover 2.

    According to recent reports, one of the coverage changeups the Bills have leaned into has been Tampa 2 invert/non traditional Tampa like the one here, with Bishop in the flat (cloud) and Igbinosun as a deep half player.     • Recent findings suggest that let's set the stage here.
    • In a recent development, did Wemby just...
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that remember at the end of Space Jam, when Michael Jordan launched himself off of the butt of a MonStar to dunk from the half-court line? Well, imagine the exact opposite of that play. Instead of an impossibly long dunk, Thursday night's NBA action gave us an impossibly short jumper.

    Recent findings suggest that let's set the stage here. The San Antonio Spurs are leading the Los Angeles Clippers by 12 points with under four minutes remaining. Victor Wembanyama is alone under the basket. He led the NBA with 71 dunks on the season to that point. Nobody else, as of the beginning of play Thursday, had reached even 50. But Wembanyama does not take this opportunity to slam down dunk No. 72, at least not intentionally. No, San Antonio's Martian with an eight-foot wingspan jumps directly in front of the basket... and flicks his wrist downward in what was seemingly a shooting motion. It swishes through the rim. Two points.

    In a recent development, did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    Officially, it will count as dunk No. 72 on the season for Wembanyama. Unofficially, as coined by Spurs broadcaster Sean Elliott, it was the first "shunk" of his season. Or, well, perhaps anyone's. It takes a perfect storm of circumstances to create a shunk: an uncommonly large basketball player, a lane open enough to ensure no defensive resistance, and perhaps rarest of all, a center disinterested in dunking.

    That begs an crucial question: what compelled this maneuver? Well, as is so often the case, necessity was the mother of invention.

    According to recent reports, wembanyama has a blister on his right hand. He doesn't know when exactly it came, but he knows where it came from. "It definitely came from dunking a lot," he told reporters after the game Thursday. The math here checks out. Wembanyama dunked 178 times in 64 games last season. That's around 2.8 dunks per game. Even if we discount the shunk, he's at 71 dunks through 16 games this season, or around 4.4.

    Fortunately for the Spurs, Wembanyama has no plans to stop dunking, "but if I can avoid it, I would," he mentioned after the win. The blister, according to Wembanyama, is quite painful. You'd hardly know it from watching him play. Wembanyama is averaging career-highs in points, rebounds, blocks and field goal percentage thus far this season. He is leading a 13-3 Spurs team that is tied for the NBA's best record thus far, and along with Luka Dončić, he is one of the two heavy favorites to win this season's MVP award.

    If he's looking for a fringe benefit here, the "shunk" might save him from the "run and just dunk" esque criticism that Giannis Antetokounmpo recevied during his MVP pursuits. This is genuine innovation in the short-distance conversion space. Innovation is rarely in short supply in San Antonio. Earlier this week, Wembanyama threw himself multiple passes off of the backboard in a single quarter. Every time you turn on a Spurs game, there's a real chance Wembanyama does something you've never seen before, and the shunk is no exception.

    #199410. Agent's Take: The Puka Nacua predicament and where his future with Rams stands after injury

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2256 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Agent's Take: The Puka Nacua predicament and where his future with Rams stands after injury

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2256 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Puka Nacua has nobody to blame but himself for a $5.77 million salary this year while playing out his four-year rookie contract.
    • It has been revealed that nacua started his career like gangbusters.
    • Sources indicate that nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns, all career highs, last season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Puka Nacua has nobody to blame but himself for a $5.77 million salary this year while playing out his four-year rookie contract. Based strictly on production, the 2023 fifth-round pick should have already become the NFL's highest-paid wide receiver ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who received a four-year contract extension averaging $42.15 million per year with a wide receiver record $120.1 million in overall guarantees in March. Instead, Nacua created his own problems.

    It has been revealed that nacua started his career like gangbusters. He set single-season rookie records with 105 receptions and 1,486 receiving yards in 2023. The receptions record has since been broken, but the receiving yards mark still stands.

    Sources indicate that nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns, all career highs, last season. The 129 receptions are tied as the seventh-best single-season total in league history, and Nacua's 107.2 receiving yards per game led the NFL last year. He also carried the ball 10 times for 105 yards with a touchdown.

    However, the Los Angeles Rams weren't comfortable giving the two-time All-Pro a massive payday during the offseason because of off-the-field problems. Nacua tried to sneak live streamers into the Rams practice facility against head coach Sean McVay's wishes late last season. During the livestream, Nacua performed a suggested touchdown dance with a gesture considered antisemitic, for which he apologized. More concerning, a lawsuit was filed against Nacua in March alleging he bit a woman while intoxicated and made antisemitic statements on New Year's Eve. Nacua spent time during the offseason in a holistic care facility to focus on personal growth and overall behavioral improvement.

    The 2026 season hasn't gone how the Rams and Nacua expected. The Rams were heavy preseason favorites to win Super Bowl LXI before the season started. A 6-4 record after 10 games didn't seem imaginable. But that's the case. Making the playoffs won't be easy, and the Rams have the NFL's hardest remaining schedule.

    Recent findings suggest that A performance comparable to 2025's, when Nacua was an NFL Offensive Player of the Year finalist, while putting his troubles behind him would have provided ammunition to push for becoming the NFL's highest-paid non-quarterback, as fellow wide receivers Justin Jefferson and Ja'Marr Chase did in 2024 and 2025 on their respective deals with the Minnesota Vikings and Cincinnati Bengals. But that distinction right now belongs to Houston Texans edge rusher Will Anderson Jr., who signed a three-year, $150 million extension averaging $50 million per year (with $134.1 million of guarantees).

    Recent findings suggest that anderson-type money is no longer a possibility. Nacua's fortunes took a turn for the worse when he suffered a sprained MCL, sprained PCL and turf toe in his right leg at the end of Week 9's win over the Washington Commanders. Nacua wasn't initially put on injured reserve, which requires a four-game absence, because the hope was he would miss about a month of action. A hip/groin problem also kept Nacua out of the Week 2 and Week 3 games.

    The off-the-field transgressions took center stage again last week when the NFL suspended Nacua three games for violating the personal conduct policy. In a controversial but not unprecedented move, Nacua is being allowed to serve his suspension while on IR. Since Nacua was already going to miss these games, the suspension is essentially just a fine of three weeks' salary costing Nacua $961,167.

    It was later revealed that Nacua is out for the season after having surgery to repair his torn MCL last Tuesday. The NFL reportedly was unaware that Nacua had undergone surgery when imposing the suspension two days later.

    According to recent reports, nacua now finishes the 2026 season with 70 catches for 715 yards with four touchdowns in seven games. He was tied for the NFL's third-most receptions and ranked seventh in receiving yards following Week 9. Nacua's 102.1 receiving yards per game are second in the league.

    The expected four- to five-month recovery time means Nacua won't be healthy before free agency begins on March 11. Speculation that Nacua has played his final game for the Rams is premature, but McVay gave mixed messages about Nacua on Monday. He stressed Nacua's importance to the team but couldn't guarantee his return next season.

    Sources indicate that it's unlikely the Rams are going to let Nacua walk out the door via the open market. The Rams would only get a 2028 third-round compensatory draft pick at best for Nacua signing with another team in free agency.

    Industry observers note that nacua appears to be destined for a franchise tag in the offseason before the 15-day designation period expires March 3. Under the NFL collective bargaining agreement's formula for non-exclusive franchise tags, the 2027 wide receiver number is projected to be 8.86% of the 2027 salary cap. That's down from this year's 9.063%.

    That means the 2027 wide receiver franchise tag should be $28.661 million, with next year's salary cap being set at $323.5 million. A 7.4% increase in the salary cap over the current $301.2 million figure would be consistent with the 7.88% growth from 2025.

    The non-exclusive tag allows a player to negotiate with other NFL teams. If an offer sheet is signed with another club, the player's team has five days to match the offer. Two first-round picks are the compensation from the signing team if the offer sheet is not matched.

    According to recent reports, an exclusive franchise tag, typically reserved for quarterbacks, is impractical due to cost. There's a different calculation in this situation: The average of the top five 2027 wide receiver salaries (salary cap numbers with some minor adjustments) at the end of the restricted free agent signing period (April 23). Initially, the non-exclusive number is used as a placeholder and adjusted upwards if the exclusive calculation dictates once restricted free agency ends.

    The 2027 exclusive wide receiver franchise tag at the moment projects to $42.247 million. Smith-Njigba's wide receiver market-setting average yearly salary is slightly below the projected tag. This number is subject to change depending on fresh wide receiver deals, contract restructures, pay cuts and/or releases between now and then.

    Industry observers note that an offer sheet is prohibited with the exclusive designation. A player under an exclusive franchise tag cannot negotiate with other teams. It is a "closed" negotiation.

    Industry observers note that franchise tag: Accommodating the non-exclusive franchise tag shouldn't be an issue. The Rams have the NFL's fifth-fewest 2027 salary cap commitments at $236.997 million with 37 players under contract and a little less than $3.83 million in existing 2026 cap space that can be carried over, according to NFLPA data. The league average is $298.84 million, with 41 players under contract (rounded to the nearest whole number).

    Sign a long-term deal: Nacua surely doesn't want to play under a franchise tag in 2027 after missing out on an opportunity to cash in this year and having another injury-plagued season. The Rams and Nacua would have until July 15 to sign a long-term deal per CBA rules. Nacua's career earnings from his rookie contract are just under $7.75 million. He also missed five games in 2024 because of a PCL sprain in his right knee, so Nacua has only played 51 games in his four NFL seasons. Playing with reckless abandon seems to make Nacua more susceptible to injury than most other wide receivers.

    It has been revealed that nacua receives an offer sheet from another team: Nacua is the type of talent a team would seriously consider signing to an offer sheet under ordinary circumstances. No wide receiver has ever been more productive than Nacua through his first 51 NFL games. Nacua's 383 receptions are the most ever during that span and 28 more than second place. His 4,906 receiving yards are bettered only by Jefferson's 4,975. Nacua's 96.2 receiving yards per game are the most in NFL history.

    However, Durability concerns and Nacua's baggage could limit offer sheet interest even though high-impact non-quarterbacks are being traded for more than two first-round picks.

    The Chicago Bears acquired All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick from the Tennessee Titans for a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fourth-round pick at the end of October. The New York Jets dealt All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner to the Indianapolis Colts for a 2026 first-round pick (16th overall), a 2027 first-round pick and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell at last year's trade deadline.

    Getting draft capital while avoiding a massive investment in Nacua may make sense for the Rams after a Super Bowl-or-bust season. After all, the 2026 and 2027 first-round picks and more were sacrificed to bring in cornerback Trent McDuffie and edge rusher Myles Garrett, the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year. A bust seems more likely since the Rams wouldn't make the playoffs if the season ended today.

    The Rams could be facing a transition year in 2027 anyway, as there could be major roster turnover. A conscious decision was made to let a stellar 2023 draft class, which includes offensive guard Steve Avila, offensive tackle Warren McClendon Jr., defensive tackle Kobie Turner, and edge rusher Byron Young, in addition to Nacua, play out their rookie contracts. Plus, future first-ballot Hall of Famer Aaron Donald ended his two-year retirement in August to return for a Super Bowl run on a one-year, $20 million deal (worth a maximum of $30 million through incentives).

    Industry observers note that other key Rams, such as wide receiver Davante Adams, offensive guard Kevin Dotson, tight end Colby Parkinson and center Coleman Shelton, will also be unrestricted free agents. Quarterback Matthew Stafford, the reigning NFL MVP, is showing his age (38) and could retire, although he signed a one-year extension for $55 million in May.

    A sign-and-trade would be more likely than an offer sheet if the Rams and/or Nacua want a fresh start. The last wide receiver to be dealt after receiving a franchise tag is Adams in 2022. The Green Bay Packers got a 2022 first-round pick (22nd overall) and a 2022 second-round pick from the Las Vegas Raiders. Adams became the league's highest-paid wide receiver on an extremely backloaded five-year deal.

    A franchise player hasn't moved for the unmatched offer sheet compensation in over 25 years. Wide receiver Joey Galloway, who received the exclusive designation, went from the Seahawks to the Dallas Cowboys in 2000 for a 2000 first-round pick (19th overall) and a 2001 first-round pick (seventh overall). Galloway signed a deal making him the NFL's then-second-highest-paid wide receiver in connection with the trade.

    It has been revealed that shortly after Adams was dealt, the Miami Dolphins acquired Tyreek Hill from the Kansas City Chiefs for five draft picks: 2022 first (29th overall), second and fourth round picks, as well as 2023 fourth and sixth round picks. Hill replaced Adams as the NFL's highest-paid wide receiver on a severely backloaded four-year contract extension as a part of the trade. Hill had engaged in more egregious conduct than Nacua. He was almost three years removed from any allegations when the Dolphins paid him.

    It has been revealed that there's a common denominator in each of these cases. A team was willing to give up significant draft capital and pay top dollar to the wide receivers.

    It has been revealed that whether Nacua remains with the Rams long-term, leaves on an unmatched offer sheet or goes through a sign-and-trade, resetting the wide receiver market isn't out of the question. That's despite missing a season's worth of games over his four NFL seasons and having non-football concerns.

    Odell Beckham Jr. also missed 17 games in his first four years, like Nacua. A broken left ankle cost Beckham the final 12 games of the 2017 season. The injuries didn't prevent the Upcoming York Giants from putting Beckham at the top of the receiver pay scale with a five-year contract extension.

    Nacua switched his representation to Win Sports Group in August, so he shares agents with Smith-Njigba. It wouldn't be surprising for Nacua's camp to seek a deal averaging at least $45 million per year, with as much as $125 million in overall guarantees plus somewhere near $95 million fully guaranteed at signing. Both guarantee marks would be new standards for wide receivers.

    In a recent development, the team that pays Nacua would be wise to insist on a team-friendly structure. This could mean fewer contract guarantees than in the top wide receiver deals and significant per-game active roster bonuses. The primary benefit of the roster bonuses is that they provide a team with some financial relief with injuries. The per-game amount is only payable if the player is on the active roster for that particular game.

    Industry observers note that the largest per-game roster bonus currently in a wide receiver contract is Christian Watson's with the Packers. Watson has $2.125 million annually ($125,000 for each game active) from 2027 through 2030.

    Industry observers note that A team making a huge financial commitment with Nacua would be betting that he isn't a buyer beware proposition. The return on investment would be poor if Nacua's problems aren't behind him or injuries continued to mount with his physical style of play.

    Joel Corry is a former sports agent who helped found Premier Sports & Entertainment, a sports management firm that represents professional athletes and coaches. Prior to his tenure at Premier, Joel worked for Management Plus Enterprises, which represented Shaquille O'Neal, Hakeem Olajuwon and Ronnie Lott.

    Damian Lillard stars in his Milwaukee return in another stark reminder of how bleak things are for the Bucks

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that MILWAUKEE -- "Stay up!
    • In a recent development, bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores.
    • It has been revealed that lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that MILWAUKEE -- "Stay up! Stay up!" The pleading voice of the Milwaukee Bucks' in-arena host was still echoing around a half-empty Fiserv Forum early on Thursday night when Damian Lillard knocked the ball away from Tyler Herro and coasted the other way for the first points of a 124-114 Portland Trail Blazers victory.

    In a recent development, bucks fans are supposed to stay standing until their team scores. Those who are still proud enough to show up and follow the tradition get much more time on their feet than they did when Lillard was still in a Bucks jersey. They waited nearly two minutes on Thursday, then spent the next two hours watching Lillard pour in a season-high 33 points to send the Bucks to their 12th consecutive defeat and an NBA-worst 1-15 record.

    It has been revealed that lillard's return to the court where he tore his Achilles a little more than a year ago -- which came just one night after the Bucks faced Giannis Antetokounmpo for the first time -- was yet another reminder of how wrong things have gone in Milwaukee over the last few years, and the grim future the franchise faces. Jrue Holiday's 22 points, seven assists and four steals on Thursday only added to the misery.

    Trail Blazers coach Micah Nori joked pre-game that this might be the "first and only revenge game" of Lillard's career. Afterward, Lillard, who was waived by Milwaukee mere weeks after his injury, downplayed its significance. It was just a normal game, he noted, "other than it just being the first time that I've played on the court since I got hurt.".

    Sources indicate that lillard's aggressiveness may have suggested otherwise, but both he and Nori attributed his approach to the Blazers being without Deni Avdija and Ja Morant. "When you're down your next two top scorers, I knew that I would need to be a little more assertive," Lillard said.

    No one knew what to expect from the 36-year-old Lillard this season after such an extended layoff, but through 15 games he's averaging 20.9 points and 4.1 assists, and shooting 35.8% from 3-point range.

    According to recent reports, "He still has the stop and go, which has made him so effective. Obviously, the jumper and his legs. I think the biggest difference would be, 18 months without playing, I don't know if you want to call it rust or timing, that's the only thing you see," Nori said pre-game. "And it's coming back. Every single day, you can see it. But when you're playing against the best athletes in the world, the best players in the world, the best defenders in the world, it is gonna take you a little bit of time to get back up to speed. But as far as from a health standpoint, you really wouldn't know it.".

    Sources indicate that the moment Lillard's Achilles snapped 572 days ago during Game 4 of a first-round playoff series against the Indiana Pacers, everyone knew it was a turning point for the Bucks. But no one could have foreseen everything that's happened since then.

    The Bucks waived Lillard not even two months after the injury and stretched the remaining $113 million on his contract over five years in order to create the cap space to sign Myles Turner to a four-year, $107 million deal with a player option for the 2028-29 season.

    "I thought it was pretty simple. I was injured. I wasn't gonna be available to play last season, and the team was focused on bringing somebody in here that they could pair with Giannis so that they could still be a competitive team, which is the business side of it," Lillard said Thursday morning at shootaround. "I saw it for what it was, and I moved on.".

    In a recent development, the desperate ploy to keep Antetokounmpo happy didn't work. Now, both he and Lillard are gone, while Turner is averaging just 7.1 points and six rebounds on 36.2% shooting this season and the Bucks are still paying Lillard $22,516,603 each year through 2030. If you break that figure down by game, they gave Lillard $247,592 for the trouble of beating them on Thursday while Turner sat and watched with a shoulder injury.

    Industry observers note that five years ago, Antetokounmpo and Holiday were carrying the Larry O'Brien trophy through the streets of Milwaukee. Three years ago, Holiday was traded for Lillard. Just over a year ago, Lillard tore his Achilles in the most recent playoff game at Fiserv Forum and was waived. Now, Antetokounmpo is leading the 9-6 Miami Heat, who sit in fourth place in the Eastern Conference, while Holiday and Lillard are together in the same backcourt for the 10-5 Trail Blazers, who occupy sixth in the Western Conference.

    Industry observers note that and the Bucks, who haven't won a playoff series since 2022 and don't own their own first-round pick until 2031, the year after they'll stop paying Lillard? They're 1-15, have the worst record in the league and are in the midst of the second-longest losing streak in franchise history. Oh, and they're also under investigation for salary cap circumvention relating to Gary Trent Jr.'s $64 million contract.

    No team has a bleaker present or future than the Bucks.

    It has been revealed that just how bad are the vibes in Milwaukee? Major Goolsby's, a sports bar down the street from the arena, has started running a new promotion on game nights: everything's free if the Bucks win.

    Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1282 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The major prize of this free agent class, ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, has landed with the Mets on a nine-year, $450 million deal.
    • The knee-jerk reaction to a contract of this size in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.
    • Sources indicate that let's stop right there.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The major prize of this free agent class, ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, has landed with the Mets on a nine-year, $450 million deal.

    The knee-jerk reaction to a contract of this size in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

    Sources indicate that let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the Mets are getting a surefire ace for nearly a decade.

    Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

    Sources indicate that since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

    The recent track record here says this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

    There isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

    According to recent reports, he's stellar. Pretty much all the time.

    Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the substantial-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

    There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

    According to recent reports, we'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a new procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

    The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

    According to recent reports, skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

    In a recent development, I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

    Recent findings suggest that again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. His nine-year deal means it'll run through his age-38 season.

    It has been revealed that for those so worried about the long-term finances of the Cohen family, are you sure you're really worried that Skubal won't be productive through five, six or even all nine years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

    A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

    In a recent development, yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

    According to recent reports, gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

    Stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

    Recent findings suggest that justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

    Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

    It has been revealed that david Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

    Industry observers note that corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

    Zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

    Industry observers note that CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

    Max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

    It has been revealed that we can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

    In a recent development, by this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:.

    Are you sure a 9-year, $450 million deal for this guy is a "risk?".

    I think we could argue that it'll be a bargain.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, brandon Aiyuk's has officially found a new NFL home.
    • Aiyuk, who was released by San Francisco on Monday, visited the Commanders on Tuesday.
    • In a recent development, according to Zenith, Aiyuk had recently been in contact with both Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and running back Rachaad White.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, brandon Aiyuk's has officially found a new NFL home. The former San Francisco 49ers receiver is signing with the Washington Commanders and will be part of the team's practice squad, CBS Sports senior reporter Matt Zenitz confirmed.

    Aiyuk, who was released by San Francisco on Monday, visited the Commanders on Tuesday. Aiyuk is joining a Washington team that has won three of its last four games and is very much in the mix in the NFC East division race.

    In a recent development, according to Zenith, Aiyuk had recently been in contact with both Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and running back Rachaad White. Aiyuk has already acquired a house in the area that's in the same neighborhood as Daniels.

    During his public spat with the 49ers in which he sought a release from his contract, Aiyuk made it abundantly clear that he preferred to sign with the Commanders. In social media posts, Aiyuk repeatedly mentioned the team, either requesting a trade to Washington or reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list with the intention of pursuing a deal with the Commanders.

    Aiyuk and Daniels got into a social media feud over the summer when Aiyuk went on a posting spree and voiced his displeasure with his situation in San Francisco, calling out Daniels and the Commanders in the process. Daniels responded by telling him to "enjoy retirement, pal," but they have since mended their relationship. Aiyuk has spoken with Daniels about the incident and apologized to him, per Zenith.

    The timing of the reconciliation also coincides with the season-ending injury to Washington wideout Terry McLaurin's.

    A 2020 first-round pick, Aiyuk hasn't played in a regular-season game since he tore his ACL and MCL during the 2024 season. The injury and a deteriorating relationship with the 49ers led to Aiyuk not playing a snap in 2025 or the first 11 weeks of this season.

    Recent findings suggest that prior to that injury, Aiyuk enjoyed a productive career with the 49ers, who selected him with the 25th overall pick in the 2020 draft. In 2022, he eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards for the first time and caught a career-high eight touchdowns. The following season, he recorded a career-high 1,342 receiving yards while helping the 49ers reach the Super Bowl.

    It has been revealed that aiyuk will now try to make an impression on the Commanders' practice squad. If that happens, the Commanders would likely add him to their 53-man roster sometime in the near future.
